Fill each cone without overstuffing, glue the top flap shut and crimp the edge with a fork.
Spray, sprinkle with garlic powder and air fry at 400 °F for 4–5 minutes. Serve with the sauce.
recipes.notes: Amounts come from the audio and on-screen captions. Macros (per pocket) are from the creator's on-screen nutrition card. He made 8 pockets with half the filling, so the full batch makes about 16. Jalapeño and yogurt amounts in the filling, and the honey/mustard in the sauce are estimates. Freezes well.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Pocket Pizza
steps: Pat dry, flatten, season with ranch mix, spray and air fry at 400 °F for 9–10 minutes. Rest 10 minutes and dice finely.
Mix the chicken with the Buffalo sauce, Laughing Cow, mozzarella, nutritional yeast, red onion and green onion.
Wet each tortilla half, add a scoop of dip in a triangle shape, fold one side then the other over it and press completely flat.
Preheat a sheet pan in the oven. Spray it, lay the 6 pockets apart, spray the tops and bake at 400 °F for 8–10 minutes until golden.
Push the slices together into a pizza, add 20 g pizza sauce per slice and the mozzarella, then broil until the cheese is golden.
recipes.notes: Amounts come from the audio. Macros (per slice) are from the creator's on-screen nutrition card. Rinsing shredded mozzarella removes the starch so it melts and stretches better.

recipes.title: Meal Prep Freezer Breakfast Burritos
steps: Mix the Buffalo sauce and sugar-free syrup.
Add the frozen peppers and onions to a hot pan (7/10), cover until softened, then uncover and sauté until browned.
Add the turkey and beef, flatten and let a crust form, cook 2 more minutes, then break up and mix with the veggies and taco seasoning.
Stir in the cottage cheese and nutritional yeast and keep mixing 10–15 minutes until thick (lower to 4–5/10 if it catches). Cool in a bowl.
In the same pan on 5/10, add the egg whites and eggs and keep the spatula moving in circles 3–4 minutes until just fluffy. Remove, then salt. Cool.
Fill each tortilla with a sixth of the meat and eggs and roll up tightly. Wrap in foil and freeze.
Unwrap, wrap in a paper towel and microwave 2½ minutes, then air fry at 360 °F for 10–12 minutes until crispy. Serve with the maple Buffalo sauce.
recipes.notes: Amounts come from the audio and on-screen captions. Macros (per burrito) are from the creator's on-screen nutrition card. The veg and sauce amounts are estimates. A low-carb tortilla cuts the calories further.

recipes.title: High-Protein Pizzadilla

items.i: burrito tortilla (or low-carb to save ~100 cal)
oregano, basil and red pepper flakes
turkey pepperoni slices (17 inside, 9 on top)

steps: Pour the egg whites into a sprayed pan and lay the tortilla on top. Cover until the egg whites set.
Carefully flip so the egg side is up.
Spread pizza sauce over half, season well with oregano, basil and chili flakes, and add mozzarella and 17 pepperoni. Fold in half while the bottom crisps.
Top with more sauce, mozzarella and 9 pepperoni, then bake at 450 °F until golden. Cut into 4 slices.
recipes.notes: Amounts come from the audio and on-screen captions. Macros (for the whole pizzadilla) are from the creator's on-screen nutrition card. The sauce amount is an estimate. The egg whites add about 22 g protein and you can't taste them; use 100 g if you prefer.

recipes.title: 108-Calorie Protein Cinnamon Rolls

items.i: keto wheat flour (e.g. King Arthur Keto)
light buttery spread (e.g. I Can't Believe It's Not Butter), melted

steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, then add the yogurt and vanilla and stir, then knead into a smooth dough.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle on the counter.
Mix the melted spread, brown sugar substitute and cinnamon into a paste and spread it over the dough.
Roll up tightly from the long side and cut into 12 rolls. Arrange in a round baking pan.
Mix the vanilla yogurt, protein powder and salt until smooth and spread over the warm rolls.
recipes.notes: Amounts and per-roll macros come from the on-screen captions (the full recipe is on his Instagram). Keto wheat flour is what keeps the carbs low; regular flour will raise them. The count of 12 rolls is from what's shown in the pan.

recipes.title: Two-Ingredient Dough Protein Cinnamon Rolls

items.i: self-rising flour (1¾ cups) — or all-purpose plus baking powder
almond milk, a little at a time

steps: Mix the flour and yogurt — keep going even when it looks dry — until it comes together, then fold, push and stretch for 3–5 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Mix the sweetener with a little molasses, the melted light butter and the cinnamon.
Roll the dough into a rectangle about 13 × 9 inches, flipping as you go so it doesn't stick.
Spread the filling edge to edge, cut into 6 long strips and roll each into a cinnamon roll.
Set on a parchment-lined tray, pour any leftover butter over the top and bake at 350 °F for about 20 minutes until golden.
Mix the protein powder with almond milk, a splash at a time, into a thick icing and spread or drizzle over the warm rolls.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the video audio; per-roll macros come from the video description. If you use all-purpose flour, add baking powder (not baking soda).

recipes.title: Thick PB Chocolate Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: vanilla Greek yogurt, plus 1 big tbsp for the respin

steps: Mix the yogurt, powdered peanut butter, protein powder and milk really well in a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on the Smoothie Bowl setting — it will look powdery, which is what you want.
Dig a hole in the middle, add a big tablespoon of Greek yogurt and Re-spin until thick and creamy.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the video; whole-pint macros come from the on-screen nutrition card. The Greek yogurt base is what makes it thick like ice cream. Freezing time not included.

recipes.title: Apple Pie Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: vanilla Greek yogurt (¾ cup), plus 1–2 tbsp for the respin
high-protein milk (e.g. Fairlife), to the fill line

steps: Cook the diced apples with cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice and a little honey until soft. Cool.
Stir the apples into the yogurt in a Creami pint, top up with milk to the fill line, mix well and freeze 24 hours.
Knock down any bulge, then spin on Smoothie Bowl. It will be powdery.
Dig a hole, add 1–2 tbsp yogurt and the broken-up Larabar, pushing it to the bottom, then Re-spin.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video. No macros were given, so all macros and the apple and honey amounts are estimates. No protein powder or pudding mix needed.

recipes.title: Almond Joy Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: cup zero-sugar toasted coconut vanilla Greek yogurt (e.g. Chobani)
bottle chocolate protein shake (e.g. Core Power), to the fill line
small handful unsweetened shredded coconut (or almonds)

steps: Mix the almond butter into the yogurt in a Creami pint, add the protein shake to the max fill line, mix and freeze 24 hours.
Sprinkle in the shredded coconut and Re-spin — no extra liquid needed.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video. No macros were given, so they are estimates.

recipes.title: Strawberry Coconut Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: cup zero-sugar toasted coconut vanilla Greek yogurt (e.g. Chobani)
high-protein milk (about ¾ cup), to the fill line

steps: Stir the strawberries into the yogurt in a Creami pint, top up with milk, mix well and freeze 24 hours.
Knock down any bulge and spin on Smoothie Bowl.
Add the coconut flakes and pecans and run Mix-In (or Re-spin for a fluffier texture).
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video. No macros were given, so they are estimates. Tastes like strawberry shortcake.

recipes.title: Blue Hawaiian Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: mango pineapple Oikos Pro yogurt drink (23 g protein)
crushed pineapple in juice, to the fill line

steps: Pour the yogurt drink into a Creami pint, froth in the blue spirulina, top up with crushed pineapple and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on Smoothie Bowl. If it's powdery, add a splash of pineapple juice or milk and Re-spin.
Sprinkle with coconut flakes or chopped pecans if you like some crunch.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video (pineapple is 'to the fill line'). No macros were given, so they are estimates. Her favorite of the four.

recipes.title: Banana Bread Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
steps: Blend the milk, banana, protein powder, cinnamon, vanilla, yogurt and maple syrup, pour into a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on Lite Ice Cream, adding a splash of milk and Re-spinning if it's powdery.
Make a hole, add the crushed graham crackers and pecans and run Mix-In.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the on-screen captions; 37 g protein for the pint is as shown. Mix-in amounts, calories, carbs and fat are estimates. Freezing time not included.

recipes.title: 2-Ingredient Banana Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
steps: Put everything in a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on Ice Cream. Re-spin with a splash of milk only if it's powdery.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video; no macros were given, so they're estimates. Tastes a bit like banana pudding.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cup Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: scoops chocolate protein powder (a little over 1)

steps: Blend everything until smooth, pour into a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on CreamiFit (or Lite Ice Cream). Re-spin with a splash of milk if powdery.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video ("over 30 g of protein"); calories, carbs, fat and the protein figure here are estimates. You can't taste the cottage cheese.

recipes.title: Low-Cal Blueberry Cheesecake Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
steps: Blend everything, pour into a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on Lite Ice Cream — it shouldn't need a re-spin.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video; under 200 calories for the pint per the creator, other macros estimated. Honest note: he found the cream cheese flavor a bit sour and didn't recommend this one — you might add more sweetener or less lemon.

recipes.title: Churro Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: milk, to the max fill line
churros or churro strips, for dipping

steps: Blend everything, pour into a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
Spin on CreamiFit (or Lite Ice Cream).
Serve with churro strips for dipping.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video; no macros were given, so they're estimates (before the churro strips). The buttery sweet dough flavoring is what makes it taste like a churro.

recipes.title: Dairy-Free Mango Coconut Sorbet (Ninja Creami)
steps: Put everything in a Creami pint and freeze 24 hours.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video; no macros were given, so they're estimates. Dairy-free; tastes like a mango lassi crossed with coconut ice cream.

recipes.title: Steak Frites with Green Herb Sauce

items.i: russet potatoes, cut into thin fries
soft herbs (parsley, chives and more), packed

steps: Parboil the cut potatoes until just tender, drain and dry. Fry once at a lower heat until pale, then again in hot oil until golden and crisp. Salt and set aside on a rack.
Blitz the shallot, garlic, lemon zest and juice, herbs, anchovies and olive oil in a small food processor into a loose, chunky sauce. Season and set aside.
Salt the steak well on all sides and sear in a ripping hot pan, pressing it down for good contact, turning until well browned.
Add the butter, garlic and herb sprigs and spoon the foaming butter over the steak until done to your liking. Rest 5–10 minutes.
Slice the steak against the grain, spoon the green sauce over it, sprinkle with green onion and pile the fries alongside.
recipes.notes: No amounts are given in the video, so all amounts and macros are estimates from what's shown. Steak is a good source of iron.

recipes.title: High-Protein BBQ Chicken Sheet Pan Pizza

items.i: no-sugar-added BBQ sauce (e.g. Sweet Baby Ray's)
pre-cooked chicken, chopped (e.g. Costco chipotle chicken)
red onion, thickly sliced and rinsed

steps: Whisk the flour, vital wheat gluten, salt and yeast in a large bowl. Pour in the warm water and stir with a spoon until it gets hard to mix, then use a wet hand to squeeze and press until all the flour is hydrated. (Shortcut: pulse the dry ingredients in a food processor for 30 seconds, stream in the water and run 45–50 seconds more.)
Cover and leave somewhere warm for 60–90 minutes. Tip: heat the oven for exactly 60 seconds, switch it off and rise the dough inside.

With a wet hand, stretch the dough up and fold it over itself, turning the bowl a quarter turn each time, until the whole dough has been folded. Flip, round it against the bowl, cover and rise another 60–90 minutes.

Spread the olive oil over a sheet pan, including the sides (add 10 g more if your pan tends to stick). Let the dough hang so it forms a rectangle, set it in the pan and press out with your fingertips to cover 70–80% of the pan. Cover and rest 15–20 minutes, then stretch it to the edges.
Spread the BBQ sauce, leaving a ½-inch border. Scatter the chicken, then the fat-free mozzarella, the part-skim mozzarella and the red onion.
Bake on the bottom rack of a 450 °F oven for 20–24 minutes until the cheese is well browned. Slice into 8, sprinkle with cilantro.
Reheat a slice in a 350 °F air fryer for 2–4 minutes.
recipes.notes: Amounts are as said in the video; per-slice macros come from the on-screen card. Shred the part-skim mozzarella yourself — pre-shredded won't melt as well. Boil the pasta in well-salted water for 1 minute less than the packet says. Drain, reserving some pasta water.

Heat a large pan until just smoking, add a little spray oil and the beef, spread it out and leave it a couple of minutes to crust. Add the herbs, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper and cook 6–8 minutes over high heat until the liquid evaporates and the beef browns.

Peel the skins off the peppers. Tip everything from the tray into a blender, squeezing the garlic out of its skins. Add the cream cheese and 35 g Parmesan and blend until smooth. Season, then thin with a little pasta water to a thick, pourable sauce.
In a large bowl, toss the pasta, beef and its juices and all the sauce. Mixing off the heat stops the cheese from splitting. Loosen with pasta water if needed.
Divide into 5 containers (about 400–450 g each), top with the remaining Parmesan and parsley. Cool 15–20 minutes before lidding.

Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Once is usually enough.
Make a hole in the middle, add the Fruity Pebbles and run Mix-In.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. One of his two favorites. Macros count roughly 10 g of the soaked cereal in the milk.

recipes.title: Crunch Bar Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
steps: Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Once is usually enough.
Make a hole in the middle, add the chopped Crunch bar and run Mix-In.
Flatten the top, spread over the melted chocolate, scatter the Rice Krispies and freeze 30 minutes to set the shell.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included.

recipes.title: Apple Pie Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: ground cinnamon and a tiny bit of nutmeg

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
steps: Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Re-spin if powdery.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. The mix is thick — blend well. Topping not included in the macros.

recipes.title: Frosted Lemonade Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: diet lemonade (Chick-fil-A or any diet lemonade)
juice and zest of ½ lemon
sugar-free fat-free white chocolate pudding mix

Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Once is usually enough.

recipes.title: 92-Calorie Watermelon Italian Ice (Ninja Creami)

items.i: juice of ½ small lime (18 g)

steps: Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Run warm water around the pint, then spin on Sorbet. It will be crumbly — run it once more on Sorbet (Re-spin).
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. Prep several pints at once for a 5-minute Italian ice any day.

recipes.title: Cosmic Brownie Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: brownie batter cookie butter protein powder

steps: Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Ice Cream. Re-spin if powdery.
Top with rainbow candy chips for the Cosmic Brownie look.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. Four layers of chocolate for a dense brownie flavor.

recipes.title: Birthday Cake Batter Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
steps: Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Once is usually enough.
Make a hole in the middle, add the sprinkles and run Mix-In.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. Use the exact amounts — the cake batter extract makes it. Sprinkle amount wasn't shown (estimated, not in macros).

recipes.title: Reese's Puffs Cereal Milk Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: Reese's Puffs cereal milk (from 56 g cereal, below)
cookie butter protein mix-in (e.g. PB Party)

recipes.title: 75-Calorie Whole-Pint Vanilla Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: your favorite cereal (he uses Lucky Charms)

steps: Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Once is usually enough.
Add a small splash of almond milk and Re-spin, then top with cereal — add more cereal as you eat down the pint.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. Not high protein — it's a very low-calorie base that leaves room for toppings.

recipes.title: Oreo Cereal Milk Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: Oreo cereal milk (from 56 g cereal, below)

steps: Soak 56 g Oreo cereal in 240 g Fairlife fat-free milk and 240 g unsweetened vanilla almond milk for 6–7 hours. Strain, pressing to get every drop — you should have about 300–330 g.
Add the base ingredients to a Creami pint and blend smooth with a small hand blender or frother. Freeze about 24 hours (lid off helps avoid a hump).
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. Once is usually enough.
Make a hole in the middle, add the Oreo Thins and run Mix-In.
recipes.notes: Amounts and whole-pint macros are from the on-screen captions. Freezing time not included. Black cocoa is what gives it the real Oreo flavor.

recipes.title: Oreo Protein Ice Cream with Greek Yogurt (Ninja Creami)

items.i: splash of milk, for the spin

steps: Stir the milk, pudding mix, protein powder and Greek yogurt together in a Creami pint and freeze overnight.
Spin on Lite Ice Cream, add a splash of milk and Re-spin if powdery.
Add the Oreo Thins and run Mix-In.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the on-screen captions (no voiceover); 41 g protein for the pint is as shown, other macros are estimates. Freezing time not included.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Chocolate Chip Pancakes
steps: Blend everything except the chocolate chips until smooth.
Pour small pancakes into a greased non-stick pan over medium-low heat, scatter chocolate chips on top, and flip once bubbles form.
Stack and top with a little extra sugar-free syrup if you like.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the video description (1 serving).

recipes.title: Chocolate Covered Banana Baked Oats
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Mix the batter ingredients until smooth and pour into a greased oven-safe dish.
Press banana slices and chocolate chips into the top.
Bake 25 minutes in a glass dish, or 17–18 minutes in a small cast-iron skillet. Finish with sea salt.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the video description (1 serving).

recipes.title: Peanut Butter French Toast Sticks
steps: Cut each slice into sticks. Whisk the egg whites, egg, milk, vanilla, powdered PB, monkfruit and cinnamon, and dip the sticks.
Cook in a greased pan over medium heat until golden on all sides.
Toss the hot sticks in monkfruit-cinnamon and dip in sugar-free syrup.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the video description (1 serving).

recipes.title: Cinnamon Roll Cottage Cheese Pancakes
steps: Blend the batter ingredients until smooth and let it rest 5–6 minutes.
Mix the applesauce, brown monkfruit and cinnamon and spoon into a zip-top bag; snip the corner.
Pour pancakes into a greased pan over medium-low heat, pipe a swirl of filling into the middle of each, then flip once set.
Stir the frosting ingredients together, pipe from a second bag over the stack, and serve.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the video description (1 serving).

recipes.title: Chocolate Covered Banana Overnight Oats
steps: Stir the oat ingredients together (except the banana), then fold in the sliced banana and pack into a jar.
Whisk the ganache ingredients until smooth and spread over the oats; top with banana slices.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the video description (1 serving).

recipes.title: Strawberry Shortcake Overnight Oats

items.i: Jell-O fat-free white chocolate pudding mix

steps: Stir the oat ingredients together, fold in the chopped strawberries and pack into a jar.
Whisk the topping ingredients until smooth, spread over the oats and finish with strawberry slices and graham crumbs.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the video description (1 serving).

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cup Pancake Bowl

items.i: Reese's peanut butter cup, chopped (half in, half on top)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Whisk the dry ingredients, then stir in the cottage cheese, yogurt, egg whites and milk.
Fold in half the chopped Reese's, pour into a greased oven-safe dish and bake about 30 minutes.
Drizzle with melted peanut butter and the rest of the Reese's.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the on-screen captions (1 serving).

recipes.title: Maple Pecan Pancake Bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Whisk the dry ingredients, then stir in the wet ingredients and the pecans.
Pour into a greased oven-safe dish and bake about 30 minutes.
Poke holes all over, pour on the maple syrup and add a Biscoff drizzle if you like.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the on-screen captions (1 serving).

recipes.title: S'mores Baked Oats
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Mix the batter ingredients until smooth.
Pour into a sprayed small cast-iron skillet and top with chocolate chips, marshmallows and graham crumbs.
Bake 18 minutes, until the marshmallows are toasted.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the on-screen captions (1 serving).

recipes.title: Biscoff Baked Oats

items.i: Biscoff spread (split between middle and top)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Mix the batter ingredients until smooth.
Pour half into a sprayed small cast-iron skillet, add a spoon of Biscoff spread, then the rest of the batter.
Bake 17–18 minutes, then top with the remaining Biscoff spread (warmed) and crumbs.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from the on-screen captions (1 serving).

recipes.title: High Protein Chicken Crunch Wraps
steps: Dice the tomatoes and shred and rinse the lettuce. Stir the yogurt with the grated garlic, salt and pepper.
Dice the chicken into even bite-size pieces and toss with all the spices, salt and pepper.
Spray a large pan over high heat, add the chicken (in batches if needed), let it sit 1–1½ minutes to crust, then cook 4–5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
On each large wrap, add 60 g yogurt sauce, 40 g lettuce, 75 g tomato, 130 g chicken, 50 g mozzarella and 3–4 nacho chips, then cover with a small wrap.
Fold the edges over in a circle, pinching each fold, and set seam side down.
Toast seam side down in a dry or lightly sprayed pan over medium heat for a couple of minutes per side until golden.
recipes.notes: Macros per wrap from the on-screen nutrition panel (43 g total carbs = 21 g net + 22 g fiber). Keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen — for meal prep, store untoasted and toast when reheating. The chips go soft in storage.

recipes.title: Biscoff Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: vanilla pudding mix (fat-free if you can find it)

steps: Blend the skim milk, almond milk, protein powder and pudding mix (plus any extras for this flavour) with a hand blender until there are no clumps.
Freeze in a Creami pint for at least 24 hours.
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. If it comes out powdery, add a splash of milk and Re-spin.
Scoop a hole in the middle, add the Biscoff spread and crushed biscuits (save a little for the top if you like) and run Mix-In.
recipes.notes: Protein and calories for the full pint as stated in the video; carbs and fat are estimates. Use a whey–casein blend — pure whey isolate won't spin as creamy. Freezing time not included.

recipes.title: M&M McFlurry Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: vanilla pudding mix (fat-free if you can find it)

steps: Blend the skim milk, almond milk, protein powder and pudding mix (plus any extras for this flavour) with a hand blender until there are no clumps.
Freeze in a Creami pint for at least 24 hours.
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. If it comes out powdery, add a splash of milk and Re-spin.
Scoop a hole in the middle, add most of the M&M's and run Mix-In; scatter the rest on top.
recipes.notes: Protein and calories for the full pint as stated in the video; carbs and fat are estimates. Use a whey–casein blend — pure whey isolate won't spin as creamy. Freezing time not included.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Oreo Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)

items.i: vanilla pudding mix (fat-free if you can find it)

steps: Blend the skim milk, almond milk, protein powder and pudding mix (plus any extras for this flavour) with a hand blender until there are no clumps.
Freeze in a Creami pint for at least 24 hours.
Spin on Lite Ice Cream. If it comes out powdery, add a splash of milk and Re-spin.
Scoop a hole in the middle, add the mini Oreos (keep a couple to crush on top) and run Mix-In. Finish with a squeeze of peanut butter.
recipes.notes: Protein and calories for the full pint as stated in the video (including the peanut butter drizzle); carbs and fat are estimates. Use a whey–casein blend — pure whey isolate won't spin as creamy. Freezing time not included. Chocolate whey also works for this one.

recipes.title: Low Calorie Double Cheeseburger

items.i: burger buns (Dave's Killer Bread, 160 cal each)
yellow or sweet onion, sliced paper-thin

steps: Whisk the mayo, mustard, sriracha, salt and pepper together — enough for four burgers.
Slice the pickles lengthwise just under ¼ in thick. Shave the onion into paper-thin rings (a mandoline helps), then rinse in cold water and drain.
Weigh the beef into eight 3 oz portions and roll each into an even ball.
Dry-toast the buns cut side down over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, then toast the outsides too.
On a very hot, well-seasoned flat top or non-stick pan, smash each ball (under parchment) about 25% wider than the bun. Season with salt and pepper.
Flip early — when the patty is about two-thirds cooked through — so the lean beef stays juicy. Add one cheese slice per burger and cook 1–2 minutes more; stack two patties per burger.
Sauce the bottom bun, add pickles, onion and the double patty, then sauce the top bun (about 1 tbsp) and close.
recipes.notes: Macros per burger as stated in the video (two 3 oz patties, one cheese slice). They only hold with 96% lean beef and the same buns.

recipes.title: Chipotle Lime Crunchwrap Supremes

items.i: guacamole or hot sauce, to serve

steps: Cook the bell pepper and onion in a hot pan until softened, then add the garlic for a minute.
Push the veg aside, add the beef and brown it, then stir in the taco seasoning.
Add the broth, green chilies and chipotle in adobo, simmer briefly, and finish with lime juice, salt and pepper.
On each wrap, spread a little Greek yogurt, then add lettuce, cheese, a quarter of the beef and a tostada on top.
Fold the edges in around the tostada and toast seam side down in a pan over medium-high heat, then flip, until golden on both sides.
recipes.notes: Macros per crunchwrap (¼ recipe) as stated in the description. The Greek yogurt appears in the video but has no amount listed.

recipes.title: 5-Minute Mango Greek Yogurt Ice Cream
steps: Add the frozen mango and Greek yogurt to a food processor, plus sweetener and protein powder if using.
Blend, stopping to scrape down the sides, until it turns completely smooth and thick like soft-serve — be patient, it takes a few minutes.
Scoop and eat right away, or freeze briefly for a firmer scoop.
recipes.notes: The video shows the ingredients without amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates (macros include the optional protein powder).

recipes.title: No-Bake Peanut Butter Chia Protein Bars

items.i: chopped pistachios, goji berries, coconut flakes, quinoa puffs or cacao nibs

steps: Line a 20 × 20 cm tin with parchment. Blitz the chia seeds in a blender for about 5 seconds to a fine powder.
Pour just enough boiling water over the dates to cover, soak 10 minutes, then mash into a spreadable paste.
Mix the peanut butter, protein powder, ground almonds, milled chia and maple syrup until crumbly, then add the water and mix about a minute into a soft, play-dough-like mass.
Press the base firmly into the tin, then spread the date paste evenly over the top.
Chill at least 30 minutes (up to an hour) until firm, then cut into 12 bars.
Melt the chocolate over a pan of simmering water. Dip each bar, let the excess drip off, and add toppings while the chocolate is still wet.
Let the chocolate set 5–10 minutes, then keep in the fridge (up to 2 weeks) or freeze.
recipes.notes: Recipe and per-bar macros from The Doctor's Kitchen website (6 g fibre per bar).

recipes.title: Chipotle Chicken & Bacon Meal Prep Burritos

items.i: chipotle hot sauce, for extra heat (optional)

steps: Pound the chicken to an even thickness, then coat well with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and chicken seasoning.
Meanwhile, cook the chopped beef bacon with the peppers in a large skillet.
Blend the cottage cheese, sour cream, chipotle peppers and enchilada sauce until smooth; add hot sauce if you want more heat.
Add the cooked chicken to the bacon pan, shred it, then stir in the sauce and the cheese. Let it cool.
Divide among 24 wraps and roll into burritos. Pack two per container (12 preps). Reheat 1 minute from the fridge, or 1 minute, flip, then 30–40 seconds from frozen.
recipes.notes: Macros per burrito as stated in the description (two burritos per prep: 485 cal, 56 g protein). The bag of Mexican cheese is added in the video but not listed in the description; amounts are as given.

recipes.title: Creamy Beef & Bacon Protein Pasta
steps: Cook the peppers and onions in a large hot skillet, then add the ground beef and break it up until browned.
Cook the beef bacon until crisp, chop it, and add it — with its fat — to the beef. The bacon is the seasoning here.
Boil the protein pasta and drain.
Blend the cottage cheese, honey, mozzarella, cream cheese, Pecorino, milk and pepper until smooth.
Add the pasta and sauce to the beef, mix, and simmer 10–15 minutes.
Divide into 10 containers (about 17 oz each). Reheat 1½ minutes from the fridge, or 1½ minutes, stir, then 45 seconds from frozen.
recipes.notes: Macros per meal as stated in the description. The video uses Fairlife fat-free milk and the description says protein milk; either works.

recipes.title: Honey Sriracha Ground Beef
steps: Whisk the sriracha, honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger and garlic together.
Sauté the onion in a large pan until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned; add the broccoli for the last few minutes.
Pour in the sauce and simmer a couple of minutes until it coats the beef.
recipes.notes: The video names the ingredients but only gives the sriracha amount (4 tbsp), so the other quantities and the macros (beef and sauce only, rice not included) are estimates.

recipes.title: 55-Calorie Air Fryer Mini Cinnamon Rolls

items.i: scoop protein powder (birthday cake or vanilla)

steps: Preheat the air fryer to 375°F. Mix the yogurt, flour and baking soda into a dough — chilling it briefly makes it easier to handle.
Stir the monkfruit, cinnamon and syrup into a paste.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface and spread the filling over it.
Roll it up lengthwise and cut into 8 pieces (unflavoured floss makes clean cuts).
Mix the glaze ingredients and pour over the warm rolls.
recipes.notes: Macros per roll as stated in the description. Recipe credited to @fitfoodieliving.

recipes.title: Pepperoni Pizza Hot Pockets (Greek Yogurt Dough)

items.i: Italian herb seasoning, garlic powder and salt

steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, Greek yogurt, herbs, garlic powder and salt until crumbly, then knead into a smooth dough ball.
Cut into 8 equal balls and flatten each as thin as you can.
Top each with 15 g pizza sauce, 20 g cheese and 20 g pepperoni.
Pinch the sides and corners into the middle to seal, flip over and press gently to flatten.
Cook in a pan on low–medium heat, lid on, 5–6 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Keep in the fridge or freezer and reheat when ready to eat.
recipes.notes: Recipe amounts and per-pocket macros from the on-screen captions.

recipes.title: 90g Protein Pepperoni Pizza (Vital Wheat Gluten Crust)
steps: Mix the flour, vital wheat gluten, yeast and salt, then slowly stir in the warm water (and oil) until a dough forms.
Knead 5–8 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover and rest 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C). Roll the dough out thin on a parchment-lined tray and bake 3 minutes.
Spread on the sauce, add the mozzarella and pepperoni, and bake about 5 minutes more until the cheese bubbles.
recipes.notes: Whole pizza: 730 cal and 90 g protein (stated, about $4.40). Per-slice carbs and fat are estimates.

recipes.title: Cheeseburger Hot Pockets

items.i: low-fat shredded cheese (25 g per pocket)

steps: Mix the flour and Greek yogurt into shaggy clumps, knead into one smooth dough, and divide into 8 balls.
Sear the beef in a hot, sprayed pan until crispy, then add the onion, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Add the stock, cream cheese, ketchup, mustard and pickles and stir until creamy.
Roll out each dough ball, add ⅛ of the beef and 25 g cheese, fold the sides in and pinch to seal. Flip and press gently to flatten.
Cook in a sprayed pan, lid on, 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Wrap and freeze; reheat when ready.
recipes.notes: Amounts from the on-screen captions; 348 cal and 31 g protein per pocket as stated. Carbs and fat are estimates, and the mustard amount was cut off on screen (1 tsp assumed).

recipes.title: Beef, Bacon & Egg Breakfast Burritos

items.i: paprika, garlic powder and onion powder
white rice, raw (cooked in 1½ cups water)
each onion powder, paprika, salt and pepper
Ole Xtreme Wellness wraps (two 6-packs — the larger size)

steps: Brown the beef with paprika, garlic powder and onion powder.
Cook the rice with 1½ cups water.
Cook the chopped beef bacon; when it's almost done, crack in the eggs, add pepper and scramble together.
Stir all the sauce ingredients together.
Mix the beef, bacon and eggs, then fold in the rice and sauce.
Divide among the 12 wraps and roll into burritos. Freeze or refrigerate for the week.
recipes.notes: Macros per burrito as stated in the description.

recipes.title: Large Protein Cinnamon Rolls

items.i: brown sugar substitute, e.g. Swerve (6 tbsp)
powdered sugar substitute, e.g. Swerve (6 tbsp)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the yogurt and brown sweetener in one bowl and the dry ingredients in another, then combine into a dough ball (add a splash of water if your protein powder makes it too stiff).
Split into two balls. On floured parchment, stretch each into a long strip about 1½ in wide, then roll up from the bottom with lightly floured hands.
Bake 11–14 minutes and let rest 15 minutes.
Mix the glaze ingredients and spoon over the rolls.
recipes.notes: Macros per roll as stated in the description (recipe makes 2).

recipes.title: Grain-Free Date-Sweetened Cinnamon Rolls
steps: Pulse the dough ingredients in a food processor until a dough forms, then chill it in the freezer while you make the filling.
Heat the oven to 350°F and line a cast-iron pan or 9-inch pie dish with parchment.
Blend the dates, cinnamon and maple syrup into a thick, syrupy paste.
Working with a third of the cold dough at a time, flatten it to about ¼ in thick, spread on filling, sprinkle with pecans and roll into a log (keep going if it cracks).
Cut into 1-inch rolls and pack them close together in the pan — they won't rise. Repeat with the rest.
Bake 35–40 minutes until the edges are golden.
Whisk the yogurt, cream cheese and powdered sugar and drizzle over the warm rolls. If you'll reheat them later, frost just before serving.
recipes.notes: Yeast-free and grain-free. Recipe, method and per-roll macros from the Hungry Hobby website.

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Date-Filled Cinnamon Rolls

items.i: warm milk, plus a little for brushing

steps: Whisk the flour and salt. Stir the yeast into the warm milk and add it, then whisk the applesauce, egg and maple syrup together and add that too.
Mix into a dough and knead until it springs back when pressed. Cover and let rise about 1 hour.
Soak the dates in hot water for a few minutes, drain, and blend with the cinnamon into a thick paste.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle, spread the date paste over it, roll it up tightly and slice into 12 thick rolls.
Arrange in a baking dish and proof 45 minutes.
Brush with milk and bake about 25 minutes at 350°F until golden.
recipes.notes: The video names the ingredients but gives no amounts or oven temperature, so quantities, the 350°F bake and the macros are estimates.

recipes.title: Mini Cinnamon Roll Skillet
steps: Combine all the dough ingredients and knead 4 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest 10 minutes.
Roll into an 8 × 10 in rectangle, spread with the softened butter and sprinkle with the brown sweetener and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly from the long edge and slice into 7 rolls.
Arrange spiral side up in a lightly greased 6-inch oven-safe skillet and bake at 350°F for 17 minutes, until golden but still soft in the centre.
Mix the frosting and spoon over the warm rolls.
recipes.notes: Whole skillet: 450 cal and 32 g protein (stated, about $1.30). Per-roll carbs and fat are estimates.

recipes.title: Low Calorie Cinnabon-Style Cinnamon Rolls

items.i: brown sugar substitute, e.g. Swerve (24 g)
powdered sugar substitute, e.g. Swerve (48 g)

steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, then add the warm water and mix thoroughly. Cover and let rise 1–3 hours at room temperature (or overnight in the fridge).
Heat the oven to 350°F. Divide into 4 balls and roll each on parchment into a 6 × 2 in strip.
Mix the syrup, brown sweetener and cinnamon, spread over the strips and roll them up.
Place in a greased or lined 8 × 8 or 9 × 9 dish and bake 21–23 minutes. Rest 15 minutes.
Stir the glaze ingredients together and spread over the rolls. Chill an hour or more for a thicker glaze.
recipes.notes: Macros per roll as stated in the description. No yeast? Swap the water for 128 g nonfat Greek yogurt (makes 3 rolls).

recipes.title: Chicken Chicharrones (Blended Chicken Chips)

items.i: chicken seasoning or spices of choice

steps: Blend the chicken breast, seasoning and baking soda into a smooth paste.
Spread onto a parchment-lined tray and press it paper-thin — put a second sheet of parchment or plastic wrap on top and flatten evenly. If it's too thick you'll get a burger, not a chip.
Bake at about 400°F until deep golden and crisp all the way through, roughly 20–25 minutes (flip or peel off the parchment partway if needed).
Break into chips and serve with a good dipping sauce.
recipes.notes: Reaction video with no amounts or oven settings shown, so quantities, the bake time and temperature, and carbs/fat are estimates; 506 cal and 89 g protein for the whole batch are as stated in the title.

recipes.title: On-the-Go Protein Pancake Bowls (3 Flavours)

items.i: scoop vanilla protein powder (a whey–casein blend bakes best)
maple syrup or sweetener of choice
Blueberry almond: blueberries and sliced almonds
Banana nut: sliced banana and walnuts (plus cacao nibs if you like)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Whisk the egg, yogurt, oat flour, baking powder, protein powder and milk until smooth, then stir in the maple syrup.
Pour into a greased oven-safe container (a glass meal-prep dish works) and top with your flavour.
Bake 30 minutes until set and golden. Make several at once for grab-and-go breakfasts.
recipes.notes: Amounts from the video for one bowl. No macros were given, so they are estimates (base batter plus a modest topping). Whey-only protein powder doesn't bake as well — they switched to Quest.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Alfredo Pasta with Blackened Chicken

items.i: garlic powder, onion powder, salt and lots of black pepper
smoked paprika, cayenne, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano and salt

steps: Season the chicken thighs with the spices and air fry until cooked through and blackened (about 12–15 minutes at 400°F).
Blend the cottage cheese, milk, Parmesan, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper until completely smooth.
Toss the pasta with the sauce over LOW heat just until warm — high heat makes the protein sauce split.
Slice the chicken over the pasta.
recipes.notes: The video gives the ingredients but no amounts; quantities, air-fry time and macros are estimates sized to the stated 70 g protein per bowl.

recipes.title: Fudgy Chocolate Protein Bars
steps: Mix the oat flour, protein powder, peanut butter powder and cocoa, then add the Greek yogurt and enough almond milk to form a thick dough.
Press evenly into a small lined tin.
Melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil and pour over the base. Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Freeze until firm, then slice into 5 bars. Keep chilled.
recipes.notes: The short shows the ingredients but no amounts or macros (the full version is on his channel), so quantities and macros are estimates. About $0.94 per bar as stated.

recipes.title: Roasted Cherry Tomato Pasta Sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Toss everything together in a 9 × 9 in baking dish.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes until the tomatoes burst and caramelise.
Smash with a potato masher for a rustic sauce, or blend until smooth.
Toss with pasta (enough for about 2 lb) and top with Parmesan and fresh basil. Refrigerate or freeze leftovers.
recipes.notes: Recipe from Tim Clowers (cookitwithtim.com), as published on Scotts Miracle-Gro. Makes about 32 oz of sauce. Macros are estimates for the sauce only, per ⅛ of the batch.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Chocolate Date Bark
steps: Split the dates open and press them flat, side by side, on a parchment-lined tray. Cover with another sheet of parchment and press into one even layer.
Spread or drizzle the peanut butter over the dates and scatter with chopped peanuts.
Pour the melted dark chocolate over the top, spread it to the edges, and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Freeze until firm, then break or cut into pieces. Keep in the freezer.
recipes.notes: Three ingredients (dates, peanut butter, dark chocolate) as named in the video — amounts weren't shown, so quantities and macros are estimates.

recipes.title: High Protein Avocado Egg Salad

items.i: salt, pepper and hot sauce (Tabasco or Cholula)

steps: Add the chopped eggs, cottage cheese, avocado and Greek yogurt to a bowl and mash together.
Stir in the red onion, cucumber, mustard and lemon juice.
Season with salt, pepper and a dash of hot sauce (jalapeño is good too) and mix well.
Pile onto toast or rice cakes, or toss with pasta. Keeps a couple of days in the fridge.
recipes.notes: The whole bowl is about 700 cal and 70 g protein as stated (split into 2 servings here); amounts weren't shown, so quantities and carbs/fat are estimates. Pictured on toast with spinach and roasted tomatoes.

recipes.title: Orange Juice Overnight Oats with Apple & Honey
steps: Stir the oats into the fresh orange juice, cover and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir in the Greek yogurt and grated apple.
Top with walnuts (and blueberries if you like) and drizzle with honey.
recipes.notes: Based on the overnight oats Princess Diana's former chef described making for her, as recreated in the video. Amounts beyond ½ cup oats and 2 oranges weren't given, so the rest and the macros are estimates.

recipes.title: Bacon & Cottage Cheese Egg Bites
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Blend the eggs, cottage cheese, Parmesan, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spray a 12-cup silicone or muffin mould and divide the bacon, peppers and onion between the cups.
Pour the egg mixture over the fillings and bake on a sheet pan about 25 minutes, until puffed and set.
Cool and refrigerate or freeze; reheat in the microwave.
recipes.notes: About 120 cal and 10 g protein per egg bite as stated. Ingredients are named in the video but not measured, so amounts, bake time and carbs/fat are estimates.

recipes.title: Watermelon Feta Arugula Salad
steps: Layer the arugula, red onion, mint, cucumber and feta in a bowl, then top with watermelon cubes and microgreens.
Whisk the mayo, olive oil, balsamic glaze and lemon juice with salt and pepper (enough for several salads).
Pack the dressing separately for meal prep and toss just before eating.
recipes.notes: One of three meal-prep salads in the video, all with the same 4-ingredient dressing. Ingredients are named but not measured, so amounts and macros (salad plus about a quarter of the dressing) are estimates.

recipes.title: Mozzarella, Tomato & Basil Arugula Salad
steps: Lay the mozzarella in the bottom of the bowl, then add arugula, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, basil and microgreens.
Whisk the mayo, olive oil, balsamic glaze and lemon juice with salt and pepper (enough for several salads).
Pack the dressing separately for meal prep and toss just before eating.
recipes.notes: One of three meal-prep salads in the video, all with the same 4-ingredient dressing. Ingredients are named but not measured, so amounts and macros (salad plus about a quarter of the dressing) are estimates.

recipes.title: Citrus, Avocado & Feta Salad
steps: Add the arugula and red onion to a bowl, top with grapefruit and orange segments, feta, avocado and microgreens.
Whisk the mayo, olive oil, balsamic glaze and lemon juice with salt and pepper (enough for several salads).
Pack the dressing separately for meal prep and toss just before eating.
recipes.notes: One of three meal-prep salads in the video, all with the same 4-ingredient dressing. Ingredients are named but not measured, so amounts and macros (salad plus about a quarter of the dressing) are estimates.

recipes.title: Perfect Air Fryer Chicken Breast (No Oil)
steps: Pick the air-fryer temperature by total chicken weight: 500 g → 180°C (355°F), 600 g → 185°C (365°F), 700 g → 190°C (375°F), 800 g → 195°C (385°F), 900 g → 200°C (390°F).
Season or marinate the whole breasts however you like — no oil needed.
Air fry 10 minutes, flip the moment the timer goes off, then cook another 10 minutes at the same temperature.
Take it out immediately and rest at least 10 minutes — it finishes cooking as it rests (cut early and it'll still be raw). Slice or shred.
recipes.notes: Timing table from the video description; follow it closely. Optional: coat in baking soda for 20–30 minutes and rinse before marinating for extra tenderness. Macros are estimates for plain chicken (about 175 g raw per serving).

recipes.title: Creamy Cajun Chicken & Rice Meal Prep

items.i: chopped parsley or chives, to garnish

steps: Melt the butter over medium heat, cook the onion and garlic until fragrant, add the Cajun seasoning and toast 1 minute, then stir in the cooked rice to coat. Set aside.
Spray the flattened chicken, coat in Cajun seasoning and cook over medium-high heat 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Slice.
In the same pan melt the butter, add the seasoning, milk and cream cheese and stir until melted, then add Parmesan and simmer on low until thickened.
Divide the rice and chicken between 4 containers and spoon the creamy sauce over the top.
recipes.notes: Amounts from the on-screen captions; 547 cal and 55 g protein per meal as stated (carbs and fat estimated). The Cajun seasoning blend for the chicken was in the caption, not shown — store-bought works.

recipes.title: 120g Protein Peanut Butter Chocolate Smoothie Bowl
steps: Blend the frozen banana, Greek yogurt, peanut butter powder, protein powder and milk until thick and smooth (add milk a splash at a time if needed).
Spoon into a bowl and top with chopped chocolate.
recipes.notes: Protein breakdown from the video: banana 1 g, yogurt 36 g, PB powder 16 g, protein powder 60 g, milk 7 g = 120 g. Calories, carbs and fat are estimates; it's a big bowl — easy to split in two. (The video says '4 tsp' PB powder but the 16 g protein matches about 4 tbsp.)

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Gochujang Chicken with Cucumber Crema
steps: Put the chicken in the slow cooker. Whisk the soy sauce, honey, broth, vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, gochujang, pepper flakes, black pepper and 2 tbsp cilantro and pour over.
Cook on low 5–6 hours, medium 4 hours, or high 2½–3 hours.
Shred the chicken in the pot, stir it back into the sauce and give it another 30 minutes on low.
Mix the yogurt, squeezed cucumber, cilantro, lime juice, garlic, salt and pepper, thin with 1–2 tbsp water and chill 15–30 minutes.
Stir in the remaining cilantro, garnish with sesame seeds, and serve over rice and cucumber with the crema drizzled on top.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the video description. 607 cal and 86 g protein per serving of chicken as stated (about $3.15); crema is 31 cal / 3 g protein per serving (makes 8). Rice not included. Carbs and fat are estimates.

recipes.title: Crunchy Rice Cake S'mores Sandwich
steps: Cover one rice cake with mini marshmallows and the other with sugar-free chocolate chips.
Air fry about 2 minutes, until the marshmallows puff and the chocolate melts.
Press the two halves together and eat warm.
recipes.notes: Under 90 cal and about 2 g protein per sandwich as stated. Amounts aren't given, so quantities and the other macros are estimates.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Protein Pancakes

items.i: melted almond butter and fresh berries

steps: Whisk the dry ingredients in one bowl and the wet in another, then combine with a spoon just until mixed.
Pour onto a buttered pan over medium heat and flip once bubbles appear on top, so both sides are golden brown.
Stack and top with melted almond butter and fresh fruit.
recipes.notes: Ingredient amounts from the on-screen cards. The title's 47 g protein is for the whole batch; per-serving macros (half the batch, toppings not included) are estimates.

recipes.title: Honey Soy Orange Salmon

items.i: salt, pepper and a little oil
roasted vegetables or grain bowl, to serve

steps: Season the salmon and sear it in a little oil for a few minutes, then flip.
Add the garlic, soy sauce and honey, basting the salmon with the pan sauce as it cooks.
Squeeze in fresh orange juice and let it bubble into a glaze.
Serve over roasted vegetables or a hearty grain bowl, spooning over the sauce.
recipes.notes: Seasoning amounts from the on-screen card; 62 g protein as stated in the title. Salmon amount and other macros are estimates (base not included).

recipes.title: Smoky Barbacoa & Rice Meal Prep

items.i: beef chuck roast, trimmed and cut into chunks (1135 g)
chipotle peppers in adobo, plus 2 tbsp adobo sauce

steps: Char the onion over an open flame or in a dry skillet; roast the garlic in its skins until soft, then peel.
Blend all the barbacoa base ingredients until smooth and brick red.
Sear the beef chunks on all sides in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, in batches.

Pour the sauce over the beef, add a splash of broth or water to nearly cover, bring to a simmer, then cover and braise at 325°F (or on a low stovetop simmer) for 3–4 hours, until it shreds easily. (A slow cooker works too, about 7 hours.)
Shred the beef, discard any large fat, stir back into the sauce and serve over rice. Adjust salt.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the video description. 648 cal and 80 g protein per serving including rice (about $3.25); carbs and fat are estimates. Shown with shredded cucumber and chipotle sauce.

recipes.title: Spinach Oat Flatbread (No Flour, No Yeast)

items.i: rolled oats, ground into flour and sifted (about 200 g), plus extra for rolling

steps: Grind the oats into a fine flour and sift.
Blend the spinach, cilantro, ginger, garlic and water until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a bowl, add the salt and stir in about 200 g oat flour gradually (add more if sticky). Add the olive oil and knead into a smooth, cohesive dough.
Roll into a log on an oat-floured surface, cut into 8 equal pieces and shape into balls. Dip each in oat flour and roll out into thin rounds, brushing off excess flour.
Cook in a hot dry non-stick pan, flipping whenever bubbles appear and pressing gently, until puffed and spotted. For extra puff, hold briefly over an open flame.
Brush with a little butter while warm if you like. Serve with garlic-mint yogurt, eggs, hummus, feta or grilled chicken.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the video description; about 130 cal per flatbread when making 8, as stated. Other macros are estimates.

recipes.title: 100g Protein Berry Banana "Giga" Smoothie
steps: Add everything to a blender — the yogurt-to-milk ratio looks off, but it blends up thick and creamy — and blend until smooth.
To cut about 200 calories, use skim milk and one scoop of protein (still about 70 g protein).
recipes.notes: Amounts from the video; 750 cal and 100 g protein as stated. Carbs and fat are estimates. Based on Joseph Abell's 'giga smoothie'.

recipes.title: Beef, Bacon & Egg Burritos with Cane's-Style Protein Sauce

items.i: Ole Xtreme Wellness wraps (two 6-packs — the large size)

steps: Brown the beef seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Chop the whole pack of beef bacon and cook it alongside.
Scramble the 10 eggs with salt and pepper in a sprayed skillet.
Stir all the sauce ingredients together.
Mix the beef, bacon, eggs, cheese and sauce in one big bowl.
Divide among the 10 wraps, fold the ends in and roll tightly, then toast seam side down until golden.
recipes.notes: Recipe and per-burrito macros from the description. In the video he also adds 40 g no-sugar ketchup and 5 g honey to the sauce instead of stevia — either works.

recipes.title: Berry Banana Almond Smoothie
steps: Add the banana, strawberries, blueberries, almonds, honey, milk and ice to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and pour.
recipes.notes: Ingredients named in the video without amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates. Add a scoop of protein powder for a higher-protein version.

recipes.title: Beef, Egg & Rice Bulking Bowl

items.i: seasonings of choice (e.g. garlic, paprika, seasoned salt)

steps: Melt the butter in a large pan, add the ground beef and seasonings, and cook, breaking it up.
Push the beef aside, crack in the eggs and scramble them into the beef.
Stir in the white rice and bell pepper until heated through.
Move to a bowl and stir in bone broth (extra protein and moisture), salsa and hot sauce.
recipes.notes: A bulking meal — about 1,800 cal and 107 g protein for the whole bowl as stated. Amounts other than the 1 lb beef and 2 eggs, plus carbs and fat, are estimates. Split it in two for a regular-size meal.

recipes.title: Crème Caramel with Marsala & Lemon
steps: Heat the 3 cups sugar with the water. Let it boil until the water evaporates and it turns a deep mahogany colour. Watch closely at the end; it goes from golden to burnt in seconds.
Ladle a layer of caramel into each ramekin and let it set. Prepare a water bath (a deep tray to sit the ramekins in).
Gently warm the milk, cream, 1 cup sugar, vanilla, lemon zest and Marsala. Whisk the eggs, temper them with a little of the warm milk, then whisk them into the rest.
Pour the custard into the ramekins over the caramel and pop any air bubbles (a quick pass with a kitchen torch works).
Set the ramekins in the water bath and bake at 350°F / 175°C for 35–40 minutes, until set with just a slight jiggle.
Cool, then refrigerate until fully set (ideally overnight).
Run a knife around the edge, place a plate on top and flip so the caramel sauce pours over the custard.
recipes.notes: The sugar amounts (4 cups total: 1 for the custard, the rest for the caramel) and 1½ cups water are from the video; the egg, milk and Marsala quantities and the number of ramekins are estimates for a restaurant-style batch. The Marsala cuts the egginess and adds sweetness. Not as sweet as it sounds.

recipes.title: 3-Ingredient Banana Yogurt 'Cheesecake'
steps: Whisk in the Greek yogurt and egg.
Pour into a small greased oven-safe dish or ramekin and bake at 350°F / 175°C for 25–30 minutes, until set (or air fry at 320°F for about 20 minutes).
Cool slightly (or chill for a firmer, more cheesecake-like texture) and drizzle with chocolate syrup.
recipes.notes: Ingredients are from the video, which gives no amounts or bake time; those and the macros are estimates for one serving.

recipes.title: Steak in a Jar (Poached with Garlic, Rosemary & Tomato)

items.i: steak (about 10 oz / 280 g), such as ribeye or sirloin

steps: Put the unseasoned steak into a wide heatproof glass jar (e.g. a mason jar). Wedge the half onion in snugly, then add the garlic, rosemary, cherry tomatoes, salt, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
Close the lid and give it a shake to coat everything.
Lay a kitchen towel in the bottom of a deep pot (so the glass doesn't touch the hot base), set the jar on it and add water to cover the jar.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 1 hour.
Carefully lift out the jar with oven mitts, let it cool a few minutes before opening, then slice the steak and spoon over the juices.
recipes.notes: A TikTok method the reviewer rated 9/10: very juicy and tender, a bit like sous vide, though without a seared crust (sear it in a hot pan afterwards if you like). The video gives no amounts; quantities and macros are estimates.

recipes.title: Za'atar Chicken & Crispy Chickpea Pita Wraps

items.i: can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and dried
each paprika, cumin and garlic powder
salt, pepper and a pinch of cumin

steps: Rub the chicken tenders with the za'atar, olive oil, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Pan-fry over medium-high heat until golden and cooked through, then chop.
In the same pan, fry the dried chickpeas with the paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt for a few minutes until crisp.
Whisk the Greek yogurt with the lemon juice, plenty of grated garlic and the spices.
Warm the pitas, spread with sauce, add the chicken, chickpeas, cucumber and red cabbage, then wrap up tightly.
recipes.notes: The video gives no amounts; quantities and macros are estimates for 2 large wraps.

recipes.title: Fluffy Protein Pancakes (4 ingredients)

items.i: vanilla / sweet cream plant protein powder (pea & brown rice blend)

steps: Whisk the protein powder, tapioca flour and baking powder, then add the egg whites and water and stir into a thick, smooth batter.
Lightly grease a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Spoon in small rounds and cook until bubbles form and the edges set, then flip and cook another 30–60 seconds.
Makes about 6 small pancakes. Top with berries and syrup or a spoon of nut butter.
recipes.notes: Macros are the creator's for the whole stack (net carbs 10 g), before toppings. The tapioca flour is what keeps them soft and fluffy. The creator used her own pea and brown rice protein (Sweet Cream; Chocolate works too) and warns other protein powders can turn rubbery.

recipes.title: Bulking Overnight Oats (941 cal)
steps: Add the oats, whole milk, protein powder, vanilla Greek yogurt, honey, chia seeds and peanut butter to a large jar and stir well.
Dice a whole apple and pile it on top.
Put the lid on and refrigerate overnight.
recipes.notes: The creator gives 941 calories; protein, carbs and fat are estimated. The yogurt amount isn't shown for this jar, so half a cup (matching the cutting jar) is assumed. See the cutting version for a lighter jar.

recipes.title: Cutting Overnight Oats (467 cal)
steps: Add the oats, almond milk, protein powder, non-fat Greek yogurt, honey and a splash of vanilla to a jar and stir well.
Add the frozen raspberries on top; they thaw overnight.
Put the lid on and refrigerate overnight.
recipes.notes: The creator gives 467 calories; protein, carbs and fat are estimated. Roughly the same size jar as the bulking version at about half the calories.

recipes.title: Chocolate Overnight Oats with Peanut-Date Milk (no milk)

items.i: fresh fruit (dragon fruit, berries or banana)

steps: Put the oats, chia seeds, cacao powder and a pinch of salt in a container.
Blend the peanut butter, 4–5 pitted dates and 1 cup water until smooth and creamy.
Pour the peanut milk over the oats, stir well, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Top with fresh fruit just before eating.
recipes.notes: Macros are estimated and exclude the fruit topping. The dates are the only sweetener; use 5 for a sweeter bowl.

recipes.title: French Toast Cloud (3 ingredients, 75 g protein)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Whisk the vanilla Greek yogurt, eggs and cornstarch until completely smooth and creamy.
Pour into a parchment-lined baking dish and bake for about 1 hour, until puffed and deep golden brown on top.
Lift out on the parchment, dust with powdered sugar and drizzle with caramel or syrup.
recipes.notes: The creator gives 75 g protein for the whole thing; calories, carbs and fat are estimated (non-fat vanilla Greek yogurt) and exclude the toppings. It's a custardy, cheesecake-like bake that tastes like French toast. Split it in two for a more typical breakfast portion.

recipes.title: Steak Sandwich with Chimichurri & Caramelized Onion Sauce

items.i: red chili, finely chopped (or chili flakes)
onion, thinly sliced (most caramelized, a little left raw and minced)

steps: Mix the parsley, chili, grated garlic, olive oil, vinegar and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Cook most of the sliced onion in butter over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and jammy.
Mix the caramelized onions with a little minced raw onion, chopped pickles, the instant coffee, mayo, ketchup, pickle juice or Worcestershire, salt and plenty of black pepper.
Season the steak well with salt and pepper. Sear in a very hot oiled pan for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, then rest for 5 minutes and slice against the grain.
Split and lightly toast the loaf. Spread the onion sauce on the bread, pile on the sliced steak, spoon over chimichurri, close and cut in half.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video shows the sauce ingredient list and the method but no amounts, so quantities and macros are estimated (per half sandwich).

recipes.title: Hot Honey Fish & Chips

items.i: flaky white fish fillets (cod or haddock), cut into pieces
each salt, black pepper, garlic powder, paprika and curry powder

steps: Salt the fish pieces and leave for 15 minutes to draw out moisture, then pat dry.
Peel the potatoes and cut into thick sticks. Boil in salted water with a splash of vinegar until just fork-tender, then drain and let them cool and steam dry.
Whisk the rice flour, flour, baking powder and spices, then whisk in the cold sparkling water until smooth and about as thick as pancake batter.
Melt the butter, toast the cayenne in it for 30 seconds, add the hot sauce, take off the heat and stir in the honey.

Heat oil to about 350°F (175°C). Fry the chips until golden and crisp. Dredge the fish in plain flour, dip in batter and fry for 4–5 minutes until deep golden; drizzle a little extra batter into the oil and scoop the crunchy bits onto the fish.
Salt everything as it comes out of the oil, then brush the fish with the hot honey.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video gives the method but not amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates (including oil absorbed while frying). The creator serves it with a spicy parmesan garlic dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Spicy Tuna Cucumber Shake Salad
steps: Thinly slice the whole cucumber straight into a large jar or lidded container (a mandoline makes this fast).
Add the mayo, tuna, Buldak sauce, sesame oil, sesame seeds, a sprinkle of furikake and a pinch of MSG if using.
Close the lid tightly and shake hard until everything is coated, then eat straight from the jar.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: amounts are eyeballed in the video, so quantities and macros are estimates. This is a take on the viral whole-cucumber salad, with tuna added for protein.

recipes.title: BBQ Potato Chip Crusted Fried Chicken
steps: Pierce the chicken all over with a fork (or a meat tenderizer) so the seasoning gets in. Add the garlic powder, smoked paprika, cumin and salt, crack in the egg and massage until every piece is coated.
Tip the chips onto a sheet tray, cover with plastic wrap and pound or roll into coarse crumbs.
Press each piece of chicken firmly into the crushed chips on both sides; the egg acts as the glue.
Shallow fry in oil at about 350°F (175°C) for 4–5 minutes per side, until deep golden and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) inside. Drain on a rack and slice.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: this is a reviewer recreating Zach Choi's viral recipe without exact amounts, so spices, quantities and macros are estimates. Thin or butterfly thick breasts so they cook through before the chip crust burns.

recipes.title: 2-Ingredient Silken Tofu Bagels

items.i: self-rising flour, plus extra for kneading

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Mash the silken tofu in a bowl, then add the flour a cup at a time, mixing and then kneading until you have a smooth, slightly tacky ball of dough.
Divide into 6 pieces, roll each into a ball, poke a hole through the middle with your thumb and stretch into a bagel shape.
Bring a pot of water to a boil with the baking soda and maple syrup. Boil the bagels one or two at a time for about 1 minute per side, then lift onto a lined baking sheet.
Sprinkle generously with everything bagel seasoning and bake for 25–30 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes: Macros are estimated per bagel, before fillings. The video says just "flour"; for a 2-ingredient version use self-rising flour, or use all-purpose flour plus 1 tbsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. The creator fills hers with vegan cream cheese.

recipes.title: Sous Vide Meal-Prep NY Strip Steaks

items.i: whole New York strip loin (about 12 lb), cut into 14 steaks

steps: Trim the strip loin and cut it into 14 even steaks.
Vacuum seal each steak (or two to a bag) with a small knob of butter and a sprig of rosemary.
Cook in a 137°F (58°C) water bath for 3½ hours; the longer cook improves the texture of the cheaper cut.
Chill the bags in ice water, then refrigerate (or freeze) until needed.
Pat a steak dry, season with salt and sear in a very hot pan for about 1 minute per side until browned.
recipes.notes: Macros are estimated per steak (about 13 oz raw). The creator works it out to about $7 a steak. Refrigerated sous-vide steaks are best eaten within about a week; freeze the rest.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Steak & Eggs with Potatoes (meal prep)

items.i: fresh garlic, minced, and fresh parsley, to finish
each salt, black pepper, cumin, paprika and garlic powder
each salt, smoked paprika and garlic powder

steps: Toss the cubed steak with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, dried parsley and olive oil. Marinate for as long as you can.
Toss the cubed potatoes with the salt, pepper, cumin, paprika, garlic powder and a little oil or spray. Oven-bake or air fry at 200°C (390°F) for 20–22 minutes until golden.
Blend the yogurt, light mayo, chipotle paste, salt, smoked paprika and garlic powder until smooth.
Heat a pan on high with the butter. Cook the steak for about 2 minutes per side until well browned, then add fresh garlic and parsley, toss and set aside.
In the same pan over medium heat, scramble the 8 eggs with salt and pepper, stirring until fluffy.
Divide the potatoes, steak and eggs between 4 containers and drizzle with the sauce. Reheat in a pan to serve.
recipes.notes: Macros are the creator's, per container. The spicy sauce keeps for weeks in the fridge, so it's worth making a double batch.

recipes.title: Beef, Egg & Cheese Breakfast Burritos with Avocado Sauce

items.i: large flour tortillas (high protein / low calorie)

steps: Mix the ground beef with the taco seasoning by hand until fully coated.
Cook in a hot pan with cooking spray, breaking it up, until browned and crispy. Stir in the tomato sauce to coat.
Blend the avocado, Greek yogurt, milk, honey, lime juice, salt and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Beat the 12 eggs. Melt the butter in a pan and scramble the eggs until light and fluffy; season with salt and pepper.
On each warm tortilla layer 2 cheese slices, 1/6 of the eggs, 1/6 of the beef, a little grated cheese and about 30 g avocado sauce.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Toast seam-side down in a dry pan until golden. Wrap in foil to store; reheat when ready to eat.
recipes.notes: The creator gives 560 calories and 62 g protein per burrito; carbs and fat are estimated and depend on your tortillas and cheese. The taco seasoning amount isn't shown, so 2 tbsp is a starting point. Despite the title, the filling is lean ground beef.

recipes.title: Classic Cocoa Hot Chocolate
steps: Warm the milk in a small pan until steaming.
Add the sugar and sifted cocoa powder and whisk until smooth. Finish with a pinch of salt; don't skip it.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe and macros (whole milk); the video gives no amounts.

recipes.title: French-Style Thick Hot Chocolate
steps: Shave the dark chocolate with a knife. Put it in a pot with the sugar, salt and cream and melt gently over low heat until glossy.
Drizzle in the milk a little at a time, whisking constantly, until thick, smooth and silky.
Pour into a cup and top with whipped cream and a little grated chocolate.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe and macros (whole milk, 70% chocolate, without the whipped cream topping); the video gives no amounts.

recipes.title: Cinnamon-Cardamom Oat Milk Hot Chocolate

items.i: oat milk, plus extra to adjust

steps: Put the chocolate, brown sugar, cinnamon stick and cardamom pods in a pot and cover with the oat milk.
Leave on very low heat for about 10 minutes so the spices infuse the milk.
Remove the spices, whisk until smooth and add more oat milk until it's as thick as you like.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe and macros; the video gives no amounts. Use dairy-free dark chocolate to keep it vegan.

recipes.title: Black Bean Chocolate Protein Bars

items.i: can (15 oz) black beans, drained (save the liquid) and rinsed
vanilla plant-based protein powder (about 60 g protein)
aquafaba (the liquid from the can), as needed
vegan chocolate chips, flaky salt and a sprinkle of cane sugar, to top

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Pulse the oats in a food processor into small bits (not quite flour).
Add the black beans, dates, protein powder, cacao powder and maple syrup. Add the aquafaba a little at a time, pulsing, until it forms one smooth dough ball.
Line a loaf pan with parchment, press the dough in evenly and top with chocolate chips, a pinch of salt and a little cane sugar.
Bake for about 20 minutes. Cool, then lift out and cut into 8 bars.
recipes.notes: Macros are the creator's, per bar. They're dense; half a bar makes a good snack. He used unsweetened chocolate chips by mistake; use sweetened dark or vegan chips.

recipes.title: Chickpea Peanut Butter Protein Bars

items.i: can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained (save the liquid)
aquafaba (the liquid from the can), as needed

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Pulse the oats in a food processor into small bits.
Add the chickpeas, allulose, protein powder, peanut butter powder and peanut butter. Add the aquafaba gradually, pulsing, until it comes together into a thick dough.
Press into a parchment-lined loaf pan and sprinkle with a little salt.
Bake for about 20 minutes. Cool, then cut into 8 bars.
recipes.notes: Macros are the creator's, per bar. They taste like a cakey peanut butter fudge; swap in chocolate protein powder for a chocolate–peanut butter version.

recipes.title: Grilled Cheese California Burrito

items.i: each onion powder, garlic powder, paprika and chipotle chili powder
avocado, mashed with salt and lime
onion, finely diced, plus chopped cilantro
shredded cheese (half inside, half for the crust)

steps: Mix the cilantro, garlic, soy sauce, Worcestershire, honey, lime juice, oil and spices. Pour over the skirt steak and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or as long as you can wait.
Put the tomatoes, jalapeños and onion in a baking dish, toss with oil, salt and pepper and roast at 425°F (220°C) until charred and soft. Blend with the cilantro, garlic and lime juice.
Cook the frozen fries until crisp (oven, air fryer or fryer).
Sear the steak in a screaming-hot cast iron pan for 2–3 minutes per side until deeply browned. Rest, then chop.
On a warm tortilla spread mashed avocado, then add steak, onion, cilantro, salsa, a pile of fries, sour cream and cheese. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Scatter a thin layer of cheese in a non-stick pan over medium heat, set the burrito on top and cook until the cheese is golden and crisp and sticks to the tortilla, turning to coat all sides.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video gives the method but no amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates. It's a big, indulgent burrito; one could easily feed two.

recipes.title: Crispy Microwave Potato Chips
steps: Slice the potato very thinly (a mandoline helps) and soak the slices in a bowl of water for about 10 minutes to rinse off the starch.
Lay the slices on a towel and pat completely dry.
Return to the dry bowl, spray with olive oil, sprinkle with salt and Cajun seasoning and toss well.

Spread in a single layer on a microwave-safe plate lined with parchment. Microwave on high for 3–10 minutes depending on your microwave (about 9 minutes in the video), checking every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros. Thinner, evenly sliced chips crisp faster; they firm up more as they cool for a minute.

recipes.title: Crying Tiger Steak over Cilantro Lime Rice

items.i: lean steak (sirloin or fillet), in 1-inch cubes
green chili (Thai or serrano), finely chopped
pinch of salt and sugar (or honey / low-calorie sweetener)
jasmine rice (dry), cooked and tossed with cilantro and lime

steps: Toss the steak cubes with soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce and black pepper. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Soak the thinly sliced red onion in ice water for a few minutes to take the harsh bite out, then drain.
In a large bowl mix the green onion, cilantro, chili and drained onion. Add plenty of lime juice, a dash of fish sauce and a pinch of salt and sugar.
Pan fry over high heat, or air fry on high for 6–8 minutes, until browned outside and pink inside.
Pile cilantro lime rice into bowls, top with the steak and spoon the herb and onion mixture over everything.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video gives the method but not amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates. Inspired by Thai crying tiger steak.

recipes.title: 450-Calorie Double Cheeseburger (45 g protein)

items.i: 96% lean ground beef, split into 2 thin patties

steps: Stir together the light mayo, sriracha, mustard, salt and pepper.

Smash the beef into two thin patties on a very hot griddle or skillet, season and cook fast, about 1–2 minutes per side. Lean beef dries out if you chase a deep crust, so pull them slightly underdone.
Put the one slice of cheese on one patty and stack the other patty on top so it melts between them; let it rest a minute.
Toast the bun, spread with sauce, add pickles and the stacked patties.
recipes.notes: The creator gives 450 calories and 45 g protein; carbs and fat are estimated and depend on your bun. The patties are good for meal prep: cook a batch slightly underdone and reheat briefly.

recipes.title: Creamy Parmesan Lemon Salmon with Mushrooms & Spinach

items.i: red bell pepper, cut into strips

steps: Make shallow diagonal slits across the salmon skin side, then again in the opposite direction to make a crosshatch. Cut into 4 fillets and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat and fry the salmon until golden brown on both sides. Remove from the pan.
In the same pan cook the onion, garlic, mushrooms and red pepper until softened, then add the spinach.
Pour in the water and heavy cream, stir in the parmesan and add the lemon slices.
Return the salmon to the pan and simmer gently for 10 minutes over low heat. Serve with the sauce spooned over.
recipes.notes: Macros are estimated per fillet (250 g raw salmon) with a quarter of the sauce. Use smaller fillets or light cream to cut the calories.

recipes.title: Butter Shrimp Tacos with Creamy Slaw & Sriracha Mayo

items.i: each chili powder, paprika and garlic powder

steps: Toss the cabbage and cilantro with the sour cream, lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Stir the mayo and sriracha together until smooth.
Season the shrimp. Melt the butter in a hot pan and cook the shrimp for 1–2 minutes per side until pink and golden.
Warm the tortillas. Fill with slaw, shrimp and avocado, drizzle with sriracha mayo and finish with cilantro.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video has no narration or amounts, so seasonings, quantities and macros are estimates based on what's shown.

recipes.title: One-Egg Japanese Soufflé Pancake

items.i: a little vanilla paste or extract (optional)
cake flour (or all-purpose or rice flour)
egg white (35–40 g, from a large egg)
lemon juice (1 tsp), or 3–4 g vinegar

steps: Whisk the egg yolk, milk, salt and vanilla, then whisk in the cake flour until smooth.
Whip the egg white with the lemon juice. Add the sugar in three additions (at about 30 seconds, 1 minute and 1½ minutes) and keep whipping to a glossy, firm meringue, about 3 minutes total.
Soften the meringue with a quick stir, then fold it into the yolk batter in parts until just combined.
Lightly oil a pan, wiping off the excess so the pancake doesn't spot. Set a 12 cm mousse ring lined with a 4–4.5 cm strip of parchment on the pan and fill with the batter.
