Cook covered over low–medium heat (about 180°C/350°F surface) for 6 minutes, carefully flip, cook 5 minutes more, then turn off the heat and leave covered for 2–3 minutes so it sets without collapsing.
Unmould and top with whipped cream, berries and mint.
recipes.notes: Macros are estimated, before toppings. The creator corrected the sugar to 20–22 g per egg (the on-screen amount was a mistake). No mousse ring? Make 2 smaller pancakes; cooking times depend on your pan.

recipes.title: Cookie Dough Baked Oats with Dark Chocolate
steps: Blend the oats, milk, banana, egg, protein powder (if using), baking powder and salt until smooth.
Pour into a deep oven-safe dish (it rises) and scatter the chopped dark chocolate on top.
Air fry at 180°C (350°F) for about 7 minutes, or bake in the oven for about 15 minutes, until puffed with a soft, cookie-dough middle. Careful, it's very hot.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video lists the ingredients but not quantities. Leave out the protein powder for a softer, lower-protein version.

recipes.title: Velveted Beef (Chinese Restaurant Tender Beef)

items.i: flank steak (or any cheap beef), sliced thin against the grain

steps: Slice the beef very thinly against the grain.
Toss with the baking soda, then add the water and massage until the beef absorbs it.
Add the sugar, chicken powder, white pepper, MSG, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine and dark soy sauce and massage everything in.
Mix in the cornstarch, then the oil, so each slice is coated. Rest for 20–30 minutes.
Sear in a very hot wok or large pan with a little oil in batches, tossing until just cooked. Use it in any stir fry.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video names the ingredients without quantities. The baking soda and cornstarch coating (velveting) is what makes cheap cuts turn ultra-tender.

recipes.title: Frozen Strawberry Yogurt Protein Clusters (chocolate-dipped)
steps: Stir the protein powder into the Greek yogurt until smooth, then fold in the chopped strawberries.
Spoon into 8 mounds on a parchment-lined board or tray and freeze until solid, about 1–2 hours.
Dip each frozen cluster in the melted sugar-free chocolate, coating completely, and return to the tray.
Freeze again until the chocolate sets. Let them sit out a few minutes before eating.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video has no narration or amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates (per cluster). Keep them in the freezer.

recipes.title: Korean Popcorn Chicken with Sticky Rice (meal prep)

items.i: sesame seeds and sliced green onion

steps: Toss the diced chicken with soy sauce, black pepper and the egg until fully coated.
Put the cornflour in a large lidded container, add the chicken, seal and shake until every piece is coated.
Spread on a rack and spray with oil. Air fry at 200°C (390°F) for 10–12 minutes, or bake at 210°C (410°F) for 10–14 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
Simmer the soy sauce, water, ketchup, gochujang, rice vinegar, honey and brown stevia, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Toss the crispy chicken in the glaze, then divide between 4 containers with the sticky rice. Top with sesame seeds and green onion.
recipes.notes: The creator gives 495 calories and 50 g protein per container; carbs and fat are estimated, and the rice amount is worked back from those calories.

recipes.title: Tender Velveted Chicken Stir Fry (homestyle)

items.i: red bell pepper, cut into strips

steps: Tenderize the chicken thighs by scoring or pounding them to break up the fibers, then cut into bite-size strips.
Add the 100 ml water and massage until the chicken absorbs it.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, white pepper and half an egg white and massage again.
Mix in the cornflour, then drizzle a little oil on top to seal it.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the chicken until golden and crisp.
Add the onion, celery and red pepper and toss over high heat, then season with oyster sauce and soy sauce (or any stir-fry sauce you like).
recipes.notes: Marinade amounts are the creator's (for 2 thighs). The vegetables and sauce are estimated from the video; he says to season it any style you like. Macros are estimated.

recipes.title: Mango Cream Mochi

items.i: toasted cornstarch or glutinous rice flour, for dusting

steps: Whisk the glutinous rice flour, cornstarch, sugar and milk into a smooth batter and strain it into a heatproof bowl.
Cover and steam for about 20 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the dough is translucent and cooked through.
While warm, knead in the butter until smooth and stretchy (wear gloves). Let it cool, then chill until firm enough to handle.
Whip the cold cream with the sugar to stiff peaks and spoon into a piping bag.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces. On a surface dusted with toasted cornstarch, roll each into a thin round.

Pipe a swirl of cream into the center of each round, add mango cubes, pipe a little more cream on top, then gather the edges, pinch to seal and place seam-side down in paper cups. Chill before serving.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video is silent with no amounts (the full written recipe is on the creator's site, u-taste.com), so quantities, times and macros are estimates for a standard mango cream mochi.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Steak from Frozen (with fries)

items.i: frozen New York strip steak (about 10 oz, 1 inch thick)

steps: Take the steak straight from the freezer and cover it generously with coarse salt on both sides (and pepper if you like).
Air fry at 400°F (200°C) for 9 minutes, flip, and cook another 9 minutes for medium. For medium-rare, try 6 minutes per side at a higher heat.
Cook the frozen fries in the second basket (or after the steak) per the package instructions.
Rest the steak for 5 minutes, then slice and serve with the fries.
recipes.notes: Macros are estimated. The 9 + 9 minute timing (from the original Iced Coffee Hour hack) gave a pink, medium center; check with a thermometer, as times vary by air fryer and steak thickness.

recipes.title: Blueberry Greek Yogurt Bake
steps: Heat the oven to 340°F (170°C). Grease or line an 8×8 inch (20×20 cm) baking dish.
Whisk the Greek yogurt, eggs, maple syrup and oat flour until smooth.
Gently fold in the blueberries and pour into the dish.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until set in the center (not jiggly) and golden around the edges.
Cool for 5 minutes before slicing. Eat warm, or chill it; it's even better cold the next day, like a light cheesecake.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, per slice. It's not very sweet, so it works as breakfast as well as dessert.

recipes.title: Three-Meat Stuffed-Crust Tortilla Pizza (850 cal, 85 g protein)

items.i: light string cheese sticks (50 cal each)
slices center-cut bacon, cooked and chopped

steps: Mix the ground beef with the egg, Italian seasoning, garlic seasoning, salt and pepper. Roll into a couple dozen small meatballs and air fry at 400°F (200°C) for about 15 minutes.
Stack the two tortillas. Lay the string cheese around the edge and fold the tortilla edge over it to make a stuffed crust.
Spread the pizza sauce, then add the mozzarella, provolone, turkey pepperoni, 2 oz of meatballs (halved) and chopped bacon.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for about 12 minutes until bubbling and the crust is crisp.
recipes.notes: The creator gives about 850 calories and 85 g protein for the whole pizza (vs ~1,800 calories for a frozen three-meat pizza); carbs and fat are estimated. You'll have leftover meatballs for other meals.

recipes.title: Gyudon (Japanese Beef & Onion Rice Bowl)

items.i: ribeye (or well-marbled beef), partly frozen and shaved paper-thin
green onions, cut into lengths, plus thin shreds to garnish
cooked short-grain Japanese rice (per bowl, about 3 cups total)

steps: Freeze the beef for 30–60 minutes until firm, then slice it as thinly as possible.
In a wide pan bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar to a simmer with the shiitake, garlic and ginger.
Add the sliced onion and simmer until soft and sweet, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef and green onion lengths and simmer just until cooked through, skimming off any foam.
Pile the beef, onions and some sauce over bowls of hot rice. Top each with an egg yolk, shredded green onion, shichimi togarashi and sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video has no narration or amounts, so the sauce follows a classic gyudon ratio; quantities and macros are estimates.

recipes.title: Turkish Pide (beef, sucuk & cheese)

items.i: each paprika and red pepper flakes
akkawi or feta-style white cheese, crumbled
shishito or long green peppers, sliced

steps: Mix the flour, salt, yeast dissolved in the warm water, and olive oil, then knead (by hand or stand mixer) into a smooth ball. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 8 equal pieces, shape into balls, cover and rest another 30–45 minutes.
Pulse the onion, bell pepper and parsley in a food processor, then mix into the ground beef with the tomato paste, red pepper paste, diced tomato, paprika, chili flakes, salt and pepper.
Mix the mozzarella with the crumbled white cheese.

Roll each ball into a thin long oval. Spread with the beef mixture, the cheese mix, or the cheese mix topped with sucuk and green peppers. Pinch the ends into points and fold the long edges over the filling.
Brush the edges with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame and nigella seeds. Bake on a tray on the very bottom of a very hot oven (about 500°F / 260°C) for 8–12 minutes until golden.
Brush the crusts with melted butter, slice and serve.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video gives the method but not amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates (per pide, averaged across the three toppings).

recipes.title: Gochujang Chicken Shirataki Noodles (299 cal pan)

items.i: pinch of salt and black pepper

steps: Drain the shirataki, rinse well under cold water and leave in a sieve while you prep.
Mix the gochujang, mirin, rice vinegar, garlic, sesame oil, ginger (if using), salt, pepper and 10–20 g water.
Heat a pan to medium-high. Add the chicken, season, cover and sear for about 90 seconds without stirring. Add the onion and stir-fry 1–2 minutes until colored, then remove everything from the pan.
Return the dry pan to medium heat and fry the noodles without oil for 2–3 minutes until all the liquid evaporates and they start to crisp.
Add back the chicken and onion, pour in the sauce and stir-fry another minute until glossy red and the chicken is cooked through.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, for the whole pan. Bulk it up for very few extra calories with carrot or cabbage.

recipes.title: Grilled Chili Lime Wings (homemade chili-lime seasoning)

items.i: dried red chiles (guajillo or ancho), stemmed and seeded
bunch cilantro, dried (or 2 tbsp dried cilantro)

steps: Soak the dried chiles in hot water until soft, then scrape out the pulp into a paste.
Spread the chile paste, lime zest and cilantro on trays and dry in a dehydrator or the oven on its lowest setting until completely dry and brittle.
Grind the dried chile, lime zest and cilantro with the salt, garlic powder and onion powder into a fine seasoning.
Pat the wings dry, toss with a little oil and coat generously in the chili-lime seasoning.
Grill over medium indirect heat, turning occasionally, for 35–45 minutes until the skin is crisp and charred in spots and the meat reaches 175°F (80°C).
Squeeze over fresh lime juice and serve.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video is music only with no amounts, so quantities, times and macros are estimates. A shortcut: use a store-bought chili-lime seasoning (like Tajín) plus extra lime zest.

recipes.title: High-Protein Crazy Puffs (tortilla pizza cups)

groups.name: For each tortilla (makes 4 puffs; the full batch is 6)

items.i: fat-free mozzarella (plus 30 g for the tops)
thin provolone slices (plus 2 for the tops)
marinara and a light garlic parmesan sauce

steps: Spread the pizza sauce over a tortilla, then add 30 g fat-free mozzarella, 2 provolone slices and the turkey pepperoni.
Roll the tortilla up tightly, brush with egg wash and sprinkle with powdered parmesan.
Cut the roll into 4 pizza puffs and stand them upright in a sprayed muffin tin or on a tray.
Spray lightly with olive oil and top with another 30 g fat-free mozzarella and 2 more provolone slices, torn.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 10 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve with marinara and garlic parm sauce for dipping.
recipes.notes: The creator gives about 750 calories and 93 g protein for 6 puffs (vs about 700 calories and 22 g protein for Little Caesars Crazy Puffs); carbs and fat are estimated. Amounts per tortilla are his; make about 1½ tortillas' worth for 6 puffs.

recipes.title: One-Pan Caramelized Onion Pasta

items.i: drizzle of olive oil (or oil from the sun-dried tomatoes)
farfalle pasta, cooked (reserve 1 cup pasta water)
handful each fresh parsley and basil, chopped

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a casserole dish toss the onions, sun-dried tomatoes, paprika, salt, pepper and dried parsley.
Set the whole garlic head in the center, drizzle with oil, cover with foil and bake for 1 hour, tossing halfway, until the onions are caramelized.
About 20 minutes before the onions are done, cook the pasta, reserving up to 1 cup of pasta water.
Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves into the dish. Add the parsley, basil, lemon juice, coconut milk, pasta and a splash of pasta water as needed. Stir and serve.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, per serving (from her PlantYou recipe card). The oven does the caramelizing for you, no stirring at the stove.

recipes.title: Scallion Oil Noodles with Fried Egg
steps: Cut the scallions into 2–3 inch segments, separating whites from greens, and thinly julienne each. Thinly slice the shallots.

Put the shallots and scallion whites in a cold wok with the oil. Cook on medium for 8–10 minutes, then add the greens and cook 5–7 minutes more until golden and crispy. Strain, keeping the oil and the crispy bits separately.
In the wok, simmer 3 tbsp of the scallion oil with the light soy, dark soy, oyster sauce and sugar on low for 2 minutes.
Boil the fresh noodles according to the package, drain and toss in the sauce until fully coated.
Plate, top with the crispy scallion bits and an egg shallow-fried in a little of the scallion oil.
recipes.notes: Recipe amounts are the creator's; macros are estimated per bowl with one egg, using about 3 tbsp of the oil (the rest keeps in a jar for other dishes).

recipes.title: Lamb Arayes with Tahini Yogurt Sauce

items.i: olive oil, plus more for cooking

steps: Grate the onion and squeeze out the liquid in a clean kitchen towel.
Mix the onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, all the spices and the olive oil, then work it thoroughly into the lamb.
Cut the pitas in half, stuff each pocket with the lamb mixture and drizzle generously with olive oil.
Sear meat-side down in a heavy pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until crusted, then toast the bread sides until golden and crisp.
Finish in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 10–15 minutes until the meat reaches about 155°F (68°C).
Stir together all the sauce ingredients, adjusting to taste, and serve with the arayes.
recipes.notes: Recipe amounts are the creator's; macros are estimated per serving with sauce.

recipes.title: Spicy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Skewers (air fryer)

items.i: boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
each paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and dried parsley
fresh parsley, chopped, plus more to serve
grated parmesan, plus more to serve

steps: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice, all the seasonings, oil, salt and pepper.
Thread onto skewers and air fry at about 400°F (200°C) for 8–10 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Mix the mayo, sriracha, mustard, garlic, red pepper flakes, parsley, lemon juice and parmesan.
Brush the sauce over the skewers while hot and top with more parmesan and parsley.
recipes.notes: Estimated recipe: the video lists the ingredients but not amounts, so quantities and macros are estimates.

recipes.title: Supreme Round Croissant with Chocolate Cream (La Fayette-style)
steps: Mix the flour and sugar with the yeast and salt on opposite sides of the bowl. Add the cold milk and water, mix, then knead in the cold cubed butter until smooth. Rest covered 30 minutes, flatten into a 30 × 20 cm rectangle, wrap and refrigerate 2 hours.
Pound and roll the cold butter between baking paper into a 20 × 20 cm square; keep cold.

Place the butter on the dough, fold the dough over to seal it in completely, then roll out and fold (letter folds), chilling between turns, to build the layers. Stretch the edges as you go to keep the layers even.
Roll the dough into a large thin sheet, trim the edges (save the scraps), and cut into long strips. Roll each strip up tightly into a spiral, brushing the end with water to seal.
Place the spirals in foil-wrapped rings (about 8–9 cm) on a lined tray. Let them rise for 2–3 hours in a warm, dark place.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 15–20 minutes, then flip upside down and bake another 15–20 minutes until deep golden on both flat sides. Cool completely.

Whisk the 100 g sugar, cornstarch, eggs and yolks. Heat the milk with the other 100 g sugar, temper it into the eggs, return to the pan and cook, whisking, until it boils and thickens. Stir in the butter and vanilla and chill.
Bring the cream to a simmer, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth. Mix some of the ganache into part of the pastry cream for a chocolate cream.
Pipe the chocolate cream into each croissant from the side, then pipe or drizzle ganache on top and finish with cacao nibs.
recipes.notes: Dough and pastry cream amounts are the creator's (from the on-screen text). The butter block, ganache amounts and macros are estimated. Bake the trimmed scraps in a muffin tin with brown sugar for bonus 'cruffins'.

recipes.title: Turkey Sausage & Hash Brown Breakfast Burritos (freezer)

items.i: large russet potato, peeled and grated

steps: Grate the potato, salt it, and squeeze out as much liquid as possible in a clean towel. Press into a lightly sprayed nonstick pan over medium heat; cook 3–4 minutes, flip and cook 3–5 more until crisp and cooked through. Set aside.

Mix the turkey with the fennel, garlic powder, cumin, onion powder, sugar and salt. Press flat into a hot sprayed skillet like a giant patty, sear 2–3 minutes, flip and cook just to 165°F (74°C). Cut into small pieces; don't overcook, lean turkey dries out fast.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet, cook the pepper and onion with salt 3–4 minutes, then add the whisked eggs and scramble until just set.
Warm the tortillas. Layer egg scramble, turkey, 1½–2 tbsp cheese, crumbled hash brown and cilantro, then roll tightly. Optionally toast seam-side down to seal.
Fridge: cool and wrap in plastic wrap for the week. Freezer: wrap, freeze, then reheat in a 400–450°F (200–230°C) oven until hot through.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, per burrito (6). Triple the batch and freeze for a month's worth.

recipes.title: Healthy Chicken Fried Rice (meal prep)

items.i: pinch of white pepper, salt and cooking spray

steps: Heat a generous amount of oil in the wok until smoking, turn off the heat, pour it out and wipe the wok clean.
Heat 1 tbsp oil until ripping hot. Spread the chicken out and sear undisturbed 3–4 minutes, flip and sear 2–3 more until browned and about 90% cooked. Remove.
Stir-fry the carrot, shallots and chilies with a little salt for 2–3 minutes until softened.
Return the chicken with the cold rice and stir-fry until the rice is hot and the chicken is just cooked through.
Push everything aside, spray the gap, scramble the 2 eggs there, then toss together with the peas, soy sauce and white pepper until hot.
Fridge for the week, or pack tightly in zip bags and freeze; reheat the sealed bag in a pot of hot (not boiling) water until hot.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, per serving (6). The rice must be cooked the day before and chilled, or it turns mushy.

recipes.title: Shrimp Coconut Red Curry (freezer-friendly)

items.i: fish sauce and salt, to taste
cooked rice, lime wedges and cilantro

steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium. Sweat the shallots, garlic and galangal with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes.
Add the curry paste and cook until fragrant and it starts to stick, then deglaze with the stock. Add the palm sugar if using.
Bring to a simmer, add the shrimp (and up to 1/2 cup water if it looks shallow), boil, then reduce to low and simmer 5–8 minutes.
Stir in the light coconut milk and lime leaves, turn off the heat and season with salt and fish sauce.
Vacuum-seal (or zip-bag) single servings flat and freeze. Reheat a frozen bag in a pot of very hot, not boiling, water for 5–10 minutes and pour over rice.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, per serving of curry (rice not included).

recipes.title: Spinach Pesto Double-Meat Panini

items.i: thin-sliced deli turkey (140 g per sandwich)
thin-sliced deli ham (140 g per sandwich)

steps: Blend the garlic, parmesan, salt, water, spinach and basil until very smooth, then stream in the olive oil. Taste for salt.
Split the buns and spread pesto on both insides. Layer 140 g turkey, 140 g ham, a slice of Swiss and a sprinkle of sun-dried tomatoes; close.
Wrap unpressed in plastic wrap and refrigerate, or freeze. Thaw a frozen sandwich at room temp about 10 minutes before pressing.
Press in a panini press or two-sided griddle at 375°F (190°C) for 5–8 minutes until flat, crisp and the cheese is melted. Cut in half.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros are the creator's, per panini using ciabatta buns; the numbers change with your bread.

recipes.title: 6 Easy Chicken Marinades (Greek lemon, cilantro lime, honey mustard, teriyaki, fajita, Italian)

items.i: limes, zested and juiced (about 1/4 cup juice)
lime, zested and juiced (about 2 tbsp juice)

steps: Pick a flavor and whisk its marinade ingredients together. Each marinade covers 1–1.5 lb of chicken.
Put the chicken in a glass container or sealable bag, pour over the marinade and refrigerate at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.
For freezer meal prep, label the bags and freeze the raw chicken in its marinade; thaw overnight in the fridge before cooking (it marinates as it thaws).
Tip the chicken and marinade into a small baking dish and bake at 425°F (220°C) for 20–25 minutes depending on size (or grill). In a larger pan, leave out most of the liquid so it doesn't burn.
Rest a couple of minutes, then slice. Cooked chicken keeps 4–5 days in the fridge for salads and bowls.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's recipe card. Her macros (per serving, a third of 1 lb) are for the Greek lemon marinade; the honey mustard and teriyaki versions run lower in fat. Only buy the ingredients for the marinade(s) you're making; untick the others in the grocery list.

recipes.title: Glazed Air Fryer Donuts

items.i: all-purpose flour, plus more as needed

steps: Mix the warm water, warm milk, yeast and 1 tbsp sugar. Let it froth for 5–10 minutes (if it doesn't, start over with fresh yeast).

In a stand mixer add the 1/3 cup sugar, melted butter, egg, yolk, vanilla, flour (spooned and leveled) and salt, then the yeast mixture. Mix with the dough hook on low until combined, then on high for 5 minutes. Add flour 1 tbsp at a time only if very sticky; it should stay slightly tacky.
Place in a greased bowl, cover and let rise in a warm place about 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch down, roll out 1/2 inch thick on a floured surface and cut with a donut cutter (or 4-inch and 1¼-inch biscuit cutters). Re-roll scraps; you'll get about 9–12 donuts plus holes.
Set on a parchment-lined tray, cover lightly and let rise 20–30 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 345°F (175°C). Spray the basket, add about 4 donuts (not touching), spray the tops and air fry 5–6 minutes. Repeat; holes need about a minute less.
Whisk the powdered sugar, milk, corn syrup and vanilla until smooth. Dip the donuts while still warm for a shiny glaze, set on a rack over a tray, and toss the holes in the remaining glaze.
recipes.notes: Recipe is the creator's; macros are estimated per glazed donut (based on 10).

recipes.title: Ham & Cheese Stuffed Eggplant with Herb Crumb
steps: Halve the eggplant lengthwise and make several deep lengthwise cuts in each half (not all the way through).
Slice the ham and cheese and tuck them into the slits.
Finely chop the basil and garlic and mix with the breadcrumbs and half the olive oil; season with salt and pepper.
Spread the crumb over both halves, drizzle with the remaining oil and scatter with parmesan.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) convection for about 30 minutes until tender and golden.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's (Riquísimo) recipe card; macros are estimated and on the rich side because of the olive oil. Use half the oil for a lighter version.

recipes.title: Eggplant Roll with Ground Beef, Ham & Cheese
steps: Cut the eggplants lengthwise into 1 cm slices and fry (or grill) on both sides until golden. Lay them overlapping on baking paper to form a base and let cool.
Mix the ground beef with the eggs, parsley, breadcrumbs, diced bread and grated parmesan; season with salt and pepper and mix by hand until even.
Spread the meat over the eggplant, leaving about 8 cm free at the top edge. Cover with a layer of ham, then the cheese slices.
Using the baking paper, roll everything up tightly, pressing so nothing escapes.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) convection for 15 minutes (until the meat is cooked through), then slice.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's recipe card (salt and pepper reduced from 1 tbsp each to 1 tsp). Macros are estimated per slice (6).

recipes.title: Eggplant Bolognese Volcanoes with Béchamel
steps: Trim a little off both ends. Stand each eggplant upright, cut around the inside leaving a 1 cm wall, and scoop out the flesh. Brush the insides with olive oil.

Brown the beef in olive oil over high heat, add the onion and garlic and keep frying. Season with salt, pepper, oregano and paprika, then add the tomatoes, tomato paste, spices and a splash of red wine if using. Simmer about 15 minutes.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk and cook briefly until thick. Off the heat, stir in the cheese, beaten eggs and salt.
Stand the eggplants on a baking tray, fill with bolognese and top each with a spoonful of béchamel.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) convection for about 20 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's recipe card; macros are estimated per stuffed eggplant. Any leftover bolognese freezes well.

recipes.title: Toad-in-the-Hole Breakfast Baguette (eggs, bacon & cheddar)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Cut 5 evenly spaced holes in the top of the baguette and scoop out some of the inside.
Cook the diced bacon until crisp and divide it between the holes, then sprinkle cheddar into each.
Crack an egg into each hole and bake about 15 minutes, until the whites are set (longer for firm yolks).
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's description; macros are estimated per egg section.

recipes.title: Bacon-Wrapped Pepperoni Cheese Baguette
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Slice the baguette lengthwise, keeping the top and bottom attached.

Spread mayo on the bottom, add 1/3 of the pepperoni, half the mozzarella, another 1/3 pepperoni, half the ketchup and the American cheese. Spread the rest of the ketchup and mayo, add the remaining pepperoni and mozzarella, and close.
Lay the bacon in one long, overlapping double row, set the baguette on top and wrap the bacon around it from both sides.
Bake for 45 minutes until the bacon is crisp. Slice to serve.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's description; macros are estimated per slice (8). Very indulgent, best for sharing.

recipes.title: Italian Sausage Meatball Sub Boat
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Mix the sausage with the garlic powder, pepper, basil, grated parmesan, egg and breadcrumbs. Shape into meatballs and fry in olive oil until golden.
Add the marinara and simmer about 15 minutes.
Cut a long rectangle out of the top of the baguette and scoop out the inside.
Sprinkle in half the mozzarella and all the shredded parmesan, add the meatballs and sauce, top with the remaining mozzarella and bake 25 minutes. Garnish with fresh basil.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's description; macros are estimated per quarter.

recipes.title: Freezer Breakfast Sandwiches (sheet-pan egg bake)
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9×13 dish and whisk in it the eggs, milk, salt, pepper and garlic powder. Stir in the broccoli, onion and pepper.
Bake about 25 minutes until set and starting to brown. In the last 5–10 minutes, bake the turkey bacon and deli meat on a sheet pan alongside.
Toast the English muffins under the broiler for a few minutes.
Cool the eggs and cut into 6 squares. Layer an egg square, 2 pieces of bacon or 1 slice of deli meat, and a slice of cheese on each muffin.
Wrap each sandwich in a damp paper towel, then parchment, and freeze in a bag for up to 1 month.
Remove the parchment, keep the damp towel on and microwave 2–3 minutes.
recipes.notes: Recipe from Tasty's recipe card; macros are estimated (their listed numbers look too low for the ingredients).

recipes.title: Freezer Smoothie Packs (4 flavors)

items.i: milk of choice (1 cup for the kiwi one)

groups.name: Pineapple orange mango fruit bag (pick one)
Kiwi banana spinach fruit bag (pick one)

steps: Put one flavor's fruit in a freezer bag, seal and freeze (up to a few months).
When ready, blend the frozen fruit with the milk and Greek yogurt until smooth. For the kiwi version, blend the milk and spinach first, then add the yogurt and fruit.
recipes.notes: Recipes and macros from Tasty's cards; macros shown are for mixed berry, per smoothie. Others: strawberry banana 258 cal / 14 g protein, pineapple orange mango 318 / 15 g, kiwi banana spinach 321 / 18 g. Buy only the fruit for the flavor(s) you're making.

recipes.title: Healthy Sheet Tray Pancakes

items.i: blueberries, strawberries, banana slices and dark chocolate chips

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Mix the flour and baking powder, then add the milk, applesauce, eggs and vanilla and stir until combined.
Spread on a greased baking sheet and add toppings all over, or a different topping in each corner.
Bake 15 minutes, cut into squares. Serve, or freeze for up to a month.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from Tasty's card (per square, before toppings).

recipes.title: Healthier Freezer Breakfast Burritos (sweet potato & turkey bacon)
steps: In a large skillet cook the turkey bacon; set aside. In the same pan cook the sweet potato with salt and pepper until soft, then the bell pepper, then wilt the spinach, setting each aside.
Lower the heat and softly scramble the eggs.
On parchment, fill each tortilla with egg, sweet potato, spinach, pepper, chopped bacon and cheese. Fold in the sides, roll tightly and wrap in the parchment.
Freeze up to 1 month. To reheat, unwrap, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave about 3 minutes; rest 1 minute.
recipes.notes: Recipe from Tasty's card; macros are estimated per burrito (their listed numbers are clearly per-ingredient, not per burrito).

recipes.title: Strawberry Chocolate Overnight Oats
steps: In a mason jar stir together the oats, milk, Greek yogurt, cocoa and maple syrup.
Add the diced strawberries, seal and refrigerate overnight.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from Tasty's card.

recipes.title: Breakfast Egg Cups (muffin tin)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Season the beaten eggs and pour into each cup about halfway, then add your choice of toppings.
Bake 20 minutes. Eat now or store in an airtight container in the fridge and reheat.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from Tasty's card (per egg cup).

recipes.title: No-Bake Almond Butter Honey Oat Bars (3 ingredients)
steps: Stir the oats, nut butter and honey together until fully combined.
Spread evenly into a dish sprayed with cooking spray.
Cover and freeze until firm, then cut into bars. Keep in the fridge.
recipes.notes: Recipe and macros from Tasty's card.

recipes.title: Banana Oat Muffin Cups (fruit-filled)

items.i: fillings: strawberries, blueberries, apple, blackberries, raspberries, almonds

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Mash the banana, stir in the egg, then the vanilla, honey, cinnamon, salt and yogurt. Stir in the oats, then the milk.
Fill each cup of a greased 6-cup muffin tin a quarter full, add a different fruit or nuts to each, then top up with the rest of the batter.
Bake 30 minutes and cool 5 minutes before removing.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's description; macros are estimated per muffin.

recipes.title: Customizable Veggie Egg Cups

items.i: fillings to mix and match: chopped spinach, diced tomato, onion, bell pepper, small broccoli florets, cheddar

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and grease a 6-cup muffin tin. Beat the eggs until smooth.
Put your chosen fillings in each cup and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the eggs over until nearly full and bake 20 minutes until set.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's description; macros are estimated per cup with a little cheese.

recipes.title: Baked Granola Cups with Yogurt & Berries

items.i: berries and other fruit or nuts

steps: Mash the banana, stir in the honey and vanilla, then the salt, cinnamon and oats.
Press about 2 tbsp into each cup of a greased muffin tin, forming a cup shape.
Refrigerate 1 hour, then bake at 350°F (180°C) for 30 minutes. Cool 5 minutes.
Add a spoonful of Greek yogurt and your favorite fruit to each cup.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the creator's description; macros are estimated per filled cup.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Lemonade Fried Chicken (Chef Chris Scott)

items.i: chicken drumsticks (or a whole chicken cut into 8)
lemon zest and flaky sea salt, to finish

steps: Whisk the brine ingredients until dissolved. Put the chicken in bags, pour over the brine and seal (vacuum-sealing pushes the flavor in fast). Refrigerate 1–4 hours.
Move the chicken to a clean container, cover with buttermilk and rest 1 hour.
Heat oil to 325°F (165°C). Combine the flour, cornmeal, cornstarch and baking powder, and dredge the chicken straight from the buttermilk.
Fry in batches without crowding, about 12 minutes, until golden and 165°F (74°C) inside. If frying mixed pieces, start with the breasts, which take longest.
Drain, rest briefly and finish with lemon zest and sea salt.
recipes.notes: Recipe from the chef's published recipe (the 'level 3' version in the video); macros are estimated per 2 drumsticks, including absorbed oil.

recipes.title: Classic French Toast (Texas toast)

items.i: slices Texas toast or thick-cut bread (about 3/4 inch)
butter and vegetable oil, for cooking

steps: In a pie plate, beat the eggs, then whisk in the milk, sugar, cinnamon, salt and vanilla until completely smooth.
Heat about 1 tsp oil and a small pat of butter over medium to medium-high heat until the butter's milk solids just start to brown.
Re-whisk the batter, then dip a slice quickly on each side (don't soak it) and let the excess drip off.
Cook without moving for about 2 minutes until golden underneath and the bubbles around the edge calm down, then flip and cook 1–2 minutes more. Add a little butter and oil between slices.
Top with maple syrup and a dusting of powdered sugar.
recipes.notes: Recipe is the creator's (2 eggs covers 6 slices); macros are estimated per 2 slices, before syrup. A quick dip instead of a soak keeps the center bready rather than custardy.

recipes.title: Pressure Cooker Pork Carnitas

items.i: white corn tortillas, guacamole, shredded cheese, cilantro and lime

steps: Wearing gloves, roughly chop the jalapeños, poblanos and serrano (seed them for less heat). Chop the onion and garlic and cube the pork.
Heat the oil in the pressure cooker over medium-high and brown the pork in small batches on all sides.
Return all the pork, then add the peppers, onion, garlic, coriander, cumin and beef broth and stir.
Lock the lid, bring up to pressure, then cook at steady medium pressure for 1 hour (about 45 minutes on high in an Instant Pot).
Release the pressure carefully, then serve as is or shred with two forks.
Pile into warm corn tortillas with guacamole, cheese, cilantro and lime, or use in burritos and enchiladas.
recipes.notes: Recipe is from the video; macros are estimated per serving of meat only. It's fairly spicy, so add or remove peppers to taste.

recipes.title: Cocoa-Nut Smoothie (chocolate, banana & almond butter)

items.i: optional: 1 scoop chocolate or vanilla protein powder

steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video lists the ingredients but the quantities are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Great after a workout; add a scoop of chocolate, vanilla or unflavored protein to boost the protein.

recipes.title: Pineapple Cream Pie Smoothie
steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.

Coconut cream (the thick fat from coconut, not coconut milk) makes it dairy-free but rich, so it's higher in calories. The creator likes it as an afternoon pick-me-up.

recipes.title: Berry Breakfast Parfait Smoothie
steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video lists the ingredients but the quantities are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). All the parts of a yogurt parfait in a glass: Greek yogurt for protein, oats instead of granola, and frozen berries so it's thick and cold without ice.

recipes.title: Green V8 Savory Smoothie
steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video lists the ingredients but the quantities are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). A green take on tomato V8, with spinach instead of lettuce. Swap a few tablespoons of the water for vegetable broth if you like it savory, and add hot sauce for a kick.

recipes.title: Sweet Green Smoothie (avocado, kiwi & matcha)
steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.

recipes.title: Orange Cream Popsicle Smoothie
steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video lists the ingredients but the quantities are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Tastes like an orange-and-cream popsicle. Turmeric gives it the bright yellow color and a gentle ginger-like warmth.

recipes.title: Berry Mint Smoothie
steps: Add everything to a blender and blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink right away.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video lists the ingredients but the quantities are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Light and refreshing; a squeeze of fresh lime really lifts the flavor.

recipes.title: Orange Ginger Sriracha Baked Salmon
steps: Stir together the orange juice, soy sauce, sriracha and ginger. Pour into a zip bag with the salmon, seal and marinate at least 30 minutes or overnight.

Heat the oven to 420°F (215°C). Place the salmon on a lined baking sheet, top with orange slices, black pepper and the remaining marinade, and bake 10–12 minutes until just opaque with a moist pink center.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros (per 6 oz fillet); the video shows the method, and full amounts are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Cooked fish keeps about 2–3 days in the fridge; freeze anything you won't eat by then. Marinating is the creator's top tip for taking away any fishy taste, and don't overcook salmon; a moist, slightly pink center is ideal.

recipes.title: Smoked Paprika & Cumin Rubbed Salmon

items.i: cilantro and lime wedges, to serve

steps: Rub the salmon with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt and pepper and cook right away (no marinating needed).
Bake on a lined sheet at 420°F (215°C) for 10–12 minutes, no more than 15.
Sprinkle with red pepper flakes and cilantro and serve with lime.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros (per 6 oz fillet); the video shows the method, and full amounts are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Cooked fish keeps about 2–3 days in the fridge; freeze anything you won't eat by then. A quick no-marinade option for salmon meal prep.

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt Dill Baked Cod
steps: Put the Greek yogurt, garlic, dill, lemon juice and pepper in a zip bag, add the cod, squeeze out the air and gently massage to coat. Marinate at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake the fillets on a lined sheet or rack for 12–15 minutes, no more than 20, until flaky.
Finish with black pepper, dill and lemon.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros (per 6 oz fillet); the video shows the method, and full amounts are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Cooked fish keeps about 2–3 days in the fridge; freeze anything you won't eat by then. Lean white fish dries out easily; the yogurt keeps it moist and adds extra protein.

recipes.title: Pecan-Crusted Baked White Fish

items.i: white fish fillets (cod or similar, 6 oz each)

steps: Crush the pecans with a mallet or spoon and mix with the panko, cumin, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Dip each fillet in beaten egg, then press into the pecan mixture.
Bake on a lined sheet or rack at 400°F (200°C) for about 15 minutes until golden and flaky.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros (per 6 oz fillet); the video shows the method, and full amounts are on the creator's site (fitmencook.com). Cooked fish keeps about 2–3 days in the fridge; freeze anything you won't eat by then. The creator made this with orange roughy but warns it's an oily fish (sold as escolar in some places) that upsets many people's stomachs, so cod or another white fish is the safer choice.

recipes.title: Muffin-Tin Meal Prep Beef Meatballs
steps: Zero a bowl on a kitchen scale, add the beef, vegetables and seasonings, and note the total weight so you can divide it evenly by the days you're prepping for.
Mix well, then weigh out 2–2¼ oz portions and roll into meatballs (about 3 make a 6 oz serving).
Bake in a mini muffin tin

Place one meatball in each cup of a mini muffin pan; they cook in their own juices, stay round and cook faster. Bake at 420°F (215°C) for 10–12 minutes (broil the last 2 minutes if you like), and don't overcook.
Simmer in marinara, crumble over salads, or serve as an after-school snack; one 2 oz meatball is a good kid-sized portion.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; full recipes are on the creator's site. Weighing everything is the creator's "exact meal prep" method for counting calories accurately.

recipes.title: Three-Flavor Sheet Pan Chicken Bites (meal prep)

items.i: boneless skinless chicken breast, trimmed and cut into nickel-size pieces
liquid aminos or low-sodium soy sauce
arrowroot starch (1 tsp for chicken, 1 tsp for sauce)

steps: Cut the chicken into small bite-size pieces, then pat very dry and let it sit on paper towels a few minutes, especially if it was frozen, so the seasoning sticks.
Toss with the onion and garlic powder, weigh it, and divide into three equal bowls.

Bowl 1: chili powder, cumin and cilantro. Bowl 2: five-spice, aminos and sesame oil. Bowl 3: toss with 1 tsp arrowroot, then coat with the Dijon, agave, water and another 1 tsp arrowroot mixed together.
Line a sheet pan with foil (or parchment) and pinch up two ridges to make three sections so the juices don't mix.
Spread one flavor in each section in a single layer and bake at 420°F (215°C) for 12–15 minutes; the small pieces cook fast.
Weigh out portions for the week; leftovers work in chicken salad, frittatas or soup.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; full recipes are on the creator's site. Small pieces cook faster and stay easier to eat even if slightly overcooked.

recipes.title: Spicy Potato Breakfast Pancakes (Indian-spiced)

items.i: red chili, seeded and finely chopped
olive oil, plus more for frying

steps: Dry-roast the cumin seeds with a pinch of salt in a non-stick pan until fragrant. Mix in a bowl with the olive oil, ginger, chili and garlic and set aside to cool.

Heat oil in a pan, add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the onion and turmeric. Add the sliced potatoes, spread them out, season and cook so they soak up the spices. Turn off the heat and let them sit.
Add the flour, salt and pepper to the cooled spice mix. Whisk in the egg, then all the milk at once, until smooth and thin; finish with 1 tsp oil for crisp edges.
Heat a large pan with a touch of oil, pour in about 1½ ladles and swirl thin. Cook until it lifts from the pan, then flip and cook until golden with crisp edges.
Lay some potato filling along one side of each pancake and roll up tightly.
Mix the coriander into the yogurt and serve on the side for dipping.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video shows the method without exact quantities. A savory, Indian-inspired breakfast that's a great use for leftover potatoes.

recipes.title: Lamb Leg Steaks with Fried Bread & Anchovy-Caper Dressing

items.i: salt and plenty of black pepper
the roasted garlic from the lamb pan

steps: Snip through the fat at each end of the steaks so they don't buckle. Season with salt and generously with pepper.

Heat a pan until just smoking, add the oil and the steaks with the crushed garlic. Hold the fatty edge against the pan to render it, then sear both sides, tilting the pan to baste with the garlicky oil. Remove and rest.
Season the diced bread and toss with milk to soak in while you make the dressing.
In a mortar, pound the roasted garlic (squeezed from its skin), anchovies and capers to a paste. Stir in the Dijon, red wine vinegar, olive oil and parsley.
Squeeze excess milk from the bread and fry in hot olive oil until golden and crisp outside, soft inside. Drain on paper towels.
Spread dressing on the plate, add croutons, stack the lamb on top and spoon over more dressing and the crispy scraps.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; the video shows the method without quantities. Lamb leg steaks are an inexpensive cut that gets big flavor from a hard sear.

recipes.title: Chorizo & White Bean Stuffed Roast Chicken
steps: Fry the chorizo in a little olive oil until it releases its oils. Add the onion, then the garlic and thyme leaves. Stir in the drained beans and semi-dried tomatoes and season well.
Trim off the knuckles and wingtips and season the cavity with salt and pepper.
Pack the stuffing firmly into the cavity to fill the space so it cooks evenly, then push in the whole lemon and pull the skin over to close.
Rub with olive oil, salt, pepper and paprika.
Put the chicken in a roasting tray with the wine, water and thyme sprigs. Cover tightly with foil and roast at 180°C (350°F) for 1 hour.
Remove the foil and roast another 30 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Squeeze the roasted lemon into the pan juices and strain. Spoon out the stuffing, carve the chicken and pour the lemony juices over.
recipes.notes: Estimated amounts and macros; oven temperature and timings are Gordon's (180°C/350°F, 1 hour covered + 30 minutes uncovered). The stuffing keeps the chicken moist and is good enough to eat as a side on its own.

recipes.title: Choco-Banana Overnight Oats
steps: Add the oats, Greek yogurt, almond milk and chia seeds to a jar with a lid. Keep the oats-to-liquid ratio 1:1.
Add the cocoa powder and agave to the jar before chilling.
Close the lid, shake well and refrigerate overnight.
Eat cold, or microwave 30–60 seconds if you like it warm, then add the toppings.
recipes.notes: Base recipe is the creator's; topping amounts and macros are estimated. Add the cocoa powder and agave to the jar before chilling. Save the banana and nuts for the morning so the banana doesn't get slimy.

recipes.title: PB&J Overnight Oats

items.i: honey, plus a drizzle to serve

steps: Add the oats, Greek yogurt, almond milk and chia seeds to a jar with a lid. Keep the oats-to-liquid ratio 1:1.
Add the peanut butter and honey before chilling; give it a stir with a spoon as well as a shake, since they're sticky.
Close the lid, shake well and refrigerate overnight.
Eat cold, or microwave 30–60 seconds if you like it warm, then add the toppings.
recipes.notes: Base recipe is the creator's; topping amounts and macros are estimated. Add the peanut butter and honey before chilling; give it a stir with a spoon as well as a shake, since they're sticky. Top with strawberries and a drizzle of honey in the morning.

Close the lid, shake well and refrigerate overnight.
Eat cold, or microwave 30–60 seconds if you like it warm, then add the toppings.
recipes.notes: Base recipe is the creator's; topping amounts and macros are estimated. Add the maple syrup and cinnamon before chilling, then top with blueberries, slivered almonds and another dash of cinnamon.

Add the flavor ingredients on top.
Close the jar, shake well and refrigerate overnight.
Eat cold straight from the fridge, or heat it up for a warm breakfast.
